Not specified for selling to clients

Objection Handling

Not specified

Contrarian Insight

Cold calling with AI is NOT allowed - you can only call leads who have previously consented to receive marketing materials. This is a legal compliance point most AI agency creators ignore. Lead reactivation specifically targets consented past clients, making it legally safe and higher-converting since they already know the business.

Mistake Warning

Do not skip the Examples section of your voice agent prompt - this is the most important part. Without good conversational examples, the voice agent goes off the rails and loses track. The Notes section should be used iteratively after testing calls to fix specific behaviors.

Scalability

System can be replicated across any service business vertical. Once the automation is built, it runs through entire lead lists automatically. Can be offered as a service to multiple clients with minimal customization (swap business details and services in the prompt).

Best Quotes

Business owners weve found dont have the time or resources to call all of these old leads, and they never end up doing it.
We are not able to send these AI generated calls to individuals that havent necessarily consented to receive any sort of marketing related information from the business. Cold calling isnt necessarily allowed.
Examples is actually one of the most important parts of your prompt. If youre unable to give it good examples, this is typically where the voice agent goes off the rails.
Notes are typically what I modify at the end of my tests. I call the agent and look at what is working well and what is not.

Action Steps

  • Use the 4-part prompt framework (Role, Task, Examples, Notes) as a template for any voice agent build
  • Always draft voice agent prompts in ChatGPT first before pasting into the voice platform - faster iteration
  • Only reactivate leads who have previously consented to marketing - never cold call with AI agents
  • Test the agent yourself first, document failures, then fix them in the Notes section of the prompt iteratively

Nick Saraev argues AI agencies are the new SMMA with a steeper growth curve, higher project values, and bluer ocean. Contrasts SMMA (red ocean, low CLV, high competition) with AI agencies (blue ocean, high CLV $15-50K, 10-15x more use cases per business). Enterprise adoption at 63% but SMBs left behind - that's the opportunity. Simple business model but NOT easy. About 1-2 weeks from being able to make money.

Pain Point

97% of businesses planning AI investment, only 21% have implemented. Business owners think AI is harder than it actually is. Big consulting firms only serve enterprise, leaving SMBs in the dust. Same pattern as website agencies in 1995 and SMMA in 2014.

Pricing Justification

AI is foundational (not just one marketing channel like Facebook). 10-15 use cases per business vs 1-2 for SMMA. Perceived hype allows premium pricing. $500B AI service economy by 2028.

Delivery Process

1. Learn AI automation fundamentals (1-2 weeks) 2. Pick SMB niche 3. Identify 10-15 AI use cases for that niche 4. Build and template solutions 5. Sell to businesses in knowledge arbitrage window 6. Deliver and retain

Tools Stack

Not specified in detail. References automation platforms, chatbots (not recommended to sell currently), voice assistants, lead generation AI.

Client Acquisition

Same as SMMA: door-knocking, cold calling, cold email, content marketing. Lower competition than SMMA.

Sales Process

Not detailed in transcript

Objection Handling

Too hard: 'You're only about a week or two away from being able to make money.' Saturated: 'SMMA is the red ocean, AI is the blue ocean with very few people and giant bags of money.' AI will replace my job: 'Be on the service side, not the displaced side.'

Contrarian Insight

Simple does NOT mean easy - in fact the simpler a model, the harder it tends to be. AI is not like the industrial revolution - it's more like the renaissance (Sam Altman). SMMA had 1-2 use cases per business (Facebook page). AI has 10-15 use cases per business (communication, decisions, logic, legal, support). Don't sell chatbots right now. This might be one of the last big economic cycles - AI is too foundational.

Mistake Warning

Thinking simple = easy. Selling chatbots (not recommended currently). Targeting enterprise when SMBs are the real opportunity. Waiting too long - the window is closing as big firms scale down to serve SMBs. Confusing the hype with sustainable business.

Scalability

Learn fundamentals (1-2 weeks) -> First SMB clients -> Template solutions -> Scale across niche -> Ride the AI hype wave pricing -> Build before window closes

Best Quotes

AI agencies are the new social media marketing agencies
Just because something is simple does not mean that it is easy
AI is not really like the industrial revolution. Sam Altman said it best - it's more like the renaissance
You're only about a week or two away from realistically being able to make a lot of money

Dan Wardrope
AI SMS Lead Reactivation (Sleeping Beauty Android)		 Lead Reactiv. Dan Wardrope demonstrates live a sales call selling his AI SMS reactivation syst Lead generation businesses, home services companies, any bus $750 deposit (refundable if no results) Performance-based: revenue share on appointments generated from reactivated leads Hundreds of thousands of SMSs sent. 30% respo Facebook groups - finding business owners looking

Full Description

Dan Wardrope demonstrates live a sales call selling his AI SMS reactivation system called the 'Sleeping Beauty Android' to a lead gen business owner. The system takes dead/unconverted leads and sends AI-powered SMS conversations to reactivate them and book appointments. 30% response rate on first SMS, roughly 10% of responders book appointments. Performance-based pricing with small deposit.

Pain Point

150 out of 200 daily leads are being lost - never contacted again. No CRM, no email follow-up, no SMS system. Sales team cant reach leads fast enough. People don't answer cold calls but respond to SMS.

Pricing Justification

100% upside for client: 150 leads/day sitting untouched are free money. 30% response rate on SMS vs near-zero on follow-up calls. 3 extra appointments per day from leads they were already losing. Skin in the game model aligns incentives.

Delivery Process

1. Get client's dead lead database 2. Build AI SMS agent trained on client's website/offer 3. Configure qualifying questions 4. Send initial 'prince charming' SMS to get response 5. AI qualifies and books appointments via SMS conversation 6. Monitor and iterate on copy/questions 7. Client provides sales script for AI refinement 8. Track attribution and revenue share

Tools Stack

AI SMS platform (custom built), client website scraping for AI training, SMS sending infrastructure, appointment booking integration, CRM for tracking

Client Acquisition

Facebook groups - finding business owners looking for leads. Warm outreach based on identified pain points. Book 'The Instant AI Agency' for framework.

Outreach Script

First SMS (Prince Charming): 'Hey, it's Sarah here from [business]. Is this the same [name] that was interested in [service]?' - Gets response first, doesn't force offer. Follow-up qualifies with 2-3 questions then books appointment.

Sales Process

1. Find prospect in Facebook group 2. Identify pain point (losing leads) 3. Share screen demo of AI SMS system 4. Let prospect interact with demo live 5. Show 30% response rate stats 6. Propose performance-based deal with small deposit 7. Close with zero-risk positioning

Objection Handling

Typing speed concern: add delays to simulate human typing. Formality: make messages shorter and more casual. How do you charge: performance-based, deposit refundable. Will people actually chat back: 30% response rate proven across hundreds of thousands of messages.

Contrarian Insight

The first SMS should NOT pitch the offer. Just get them to say 'yes' to confirm identity. People in 2025 prefer SMS over phone calls. Don't qualify heavily upfront if response rates drop - get them to appointment faster. Copywriting skills + AI = unstoppable combination for lead reactivation. The deposit is just skin-in-the-game, fully refundable.

Mistake Warning

Making AI messages too long and formal. Not adding typing delays (dead giveaway it's AI). Qualifying too aggressively before booking. Not getting client's actual sales script to train the AI. Starting without a deposit (client needs skin in the game).

Scalability

Demo to one client -> Prove 30% response rate -> Performance deal -> Replicate for any industry with dead leads -> Blue ocean opportunity across all businesses with databases

Best Quotes

30% of people that we send this message to respond. 30%
Out of 150 leads you're not talking to each day, probably 40 will respond to this message
It's performance based. We'd want some skin in the game from you
If we didn't get any results, we'd refund the money

Action Steps

  • Build an AI SMS reactivation demo for one industry
  • Write a 'prince charming' first message that gets identity confirmation
  • Test with 100 dead leads to validate 30% response rate
  • Create a performance-based pricing proposal template
  • Find 5 businesses in Facebook groups with large unconverted lead databases

Cold email probably single-handedly is the highest success rate business model for any beginner maybe of all time
You just like prompted AI and had it spit some stuff out without fundamentally understanding what youre saying - thats what I actively teach against

  • Kill sunk cost thinking - pivot immediately when a better path is clear

32 Sales Calls in 1 Week (AI Agent Build)		 Chatbot Jordan Platten rebuilds the AI agent that generated 32 sales calls in one week f Any business generating leads through paid ads, lead magnets Sells this as a service for at least $2,000 in his agency Included in agency retainer or standalone AI service 32 sales calls booked in one week. 675 GBP pe Lead magnets (cold calling scripts), paid ads, You

Full Description

Jordan Platten rebuilds the AI agent that generated 32 sales calls in one week for his agency. Uses Appointwise platform for SMS/WhatsApp/Instagram/Facebook-based AI conversations that qualify leads, handle objections, and book appointments automatically. Two demos: simple outbound agent for solar company, and complex inbound agent with lead magnet delivery and multi-product segmentation. Each booked call worth 675 GBP based on 20% close rate.

Pain Point

SDR team can't reach leads fast enough. Leads go cold while waiting for human follow-up. Multiple product offerings require complex segmentation. Humans sleep but leads come in 24/7.

Pricing Justification

196 leads -> 164 activated -> 32 booked calls in one week. Each call worth 675 GBP (20% close rate x $4-20K products). ROI is immediate and measurable.

Delivery Process

1. Set up Appointwise agent (website scan auto-generates prompt) 2. Configure tonality, message delay, qualification priority 3. Set qualifying questions (1-3 max for simple, more for complex) 4. Configure follow-ups (5-10, including 30-day nurture) 5. Connect calendar (Google, GoHighLevel, Zapier) 6. Set AI tasks (tag unqualified, escalate high-value) 7. Import leads from CRM 8. AI sends outbound messages and handles inbound 9. Monitor via testing window

Tools Stack

Appointwise (AI sales agent platform - SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook), GoHighLevel (CRM), Google Calendar, Zapier (integration), Clay.com (lead gen - Jordan is investor), School.com (community), Triple Whale (attribution)

Client Acquisition

Lead magnets (cold calling scripts), paid ads, YouTube content, Instagram DMs. AI agent handles all follow-up.

Outreach Script

AI outbound: 'Hey, it's [name] from [company]. Can you confirm this is [first_name]? Just checking, are you still interested in a free quote for solar? What made you curious about solar - bills, environment, something else? Do you own your property or rent?' Inbound lead magnet: qualifies before sending resource, then segments to appropriate product/calendar.

Sales Process

1. Lead enters through ad/lead magnet/DM 2. AI activates and sends first message 3. AI qualifies with 1-3 questions 4. AI handles objections conversationally 5. AI books call on appropriate calendar 6. Follow-ups continue for non-responders (5-10 messages over 30 days) 7. AI tags and segments in CRM based on responses

Objection Handling

Example from live conversation: Lead says 'I'm pretty happy where I'm at.' AI: 'I get that. You've achieved a lot already, but there's always room for growth, right? Would you be up for a quick call to explore how we can help with a game plan for launching those paid ads?' Lead pushes back on timing: AI offers alternative time. Pressure test: 'Can you cut to the chase?' AI: 'Understood. Let me get you booked.'

Contrarian Insight

Have 1-3 qualifying questions max for simple outbound. Follow up for 30 days, not just 5. Keep qualification priority on 'conservative' - don't push too hard for answers. Let the AI objection-handle - it's better than most humans at staying calm and persistent. 84% activation rate proves AI follow-up drastically outperforms human SDR teams.

Mistake Warning

Too many qualifying questions (causes drop-off). Not enough follow-ups (stop at 5 when 10+ over 30 days works better). Setting qualification priority too aggressive. Not testing the agent before deploying. Forgetting to set up CRM tags for different outcomes.

Scalability

Build for own business -> Prove results (32 calls/week) -> Sell as $2K+ service -> Scale across client base -> Platform investment/partnership

Best Quotes

32 sales calls booked in one week completely automatically without my intervention
This is a service we sell for at least $2,000 in my agency
Each of those sales calls is worth to us 675 pounds because our close rate is roughly 20%
I get that. You've achieved a lot already, but there's always room for growth, right?

Action Steps

  • Set up an AI sales agent for your own lead follow-up first
  • Import your unconverted leads and test activation rate
  • Configure 1-3 qualifying questions and 10 follow-up messages over 30 days
  • Track: activation rate, qualification rate, booked call rate
  • Once proven, package as $2K+ service for clients

The creator ev Companies, creators, and entrepreneurs who need consistent h Not specified for new agency £3,500 retainers (evolved from £50 one-off to £250 one-off to £3,500/month retainer) Scaled traditional content agency to multiple Cold DMs (originally), personal brand content on Y

Full Description

Documentary series on building an AI content agency from scratch. The creator evolved from traditional SMMA to content agency to AI-powered content agency. Original content agency scaled to multiple clients with large team of editors, scriptwriters, and social media managers but suffered from terrible profit margins and burnout. Invested savings into building Fusion AI - an all-in-one AI content system that handles scripting, ideation, editing, and social media management. Reduced team from large to handful of people. Now documenting the process of starting a new AI content agency from zero to show others how to replicate.

Pain Point

Traditional content agencies require huge teams (editors, scriptwriters, social media managers) leading to low profit margins. Every 3 clients requires hiring a new editor. Business owners are chained to their laptops managing teams. AI solves the labor-intensive fulfillment problem.

Pricing Justification

AI handles 80% of the work - scripting, ideation, editing. Dramatically reduced team size means near-100% margins minus software costs vs. the old model where every 3 clients required a new hire.

Delivery Process

1. Sign client for content management. 2. Use Fusion AI for scripting, ideation, and editing. 3. Content manager (one person) handles entire content process for all agency clients. 4. AI handles 80% of fulfillment work. 5. Deliver consistent content across clients platforms.

Tools Stack

Fusion AI (proprietary all-in-one AI content system - handles scripting, ideation, editing, social media management), Canva (previously), Stripe (payments), Slack (team communication). Previously used large team of VAs, editors, scriptwriters, thumbnail designers, social media managers.

Client Acquisition

Cold DMs (originally), personal brand content on YouTube channel, referrals from results. Series documents building from zero using personal brand + AI content.

Outreach Script

Not specified in first 12K chars - series documents the process from episode 1

Sales Process

Not specified in first episode - upcoming in series

Objection Handling

Addresses no prior experience needed because AI handles 80% of work. Transparency about Fusion AI not being launched yet (waitlist only) to prove its not a cash grab.

Contrarian Insight

The traditional content agency model is broken - it doesnt scale because every 3 clients requires a new hire, margins are terrible, and the business owns you. The fix isnt better management, its replacing 80% of the labor with AI. You need no experience because AI handles the fulfillment.

Mistake Warning

Scaling a content agency by hiring more people is a trap. Revenue grows but profit margins shrink, complexity explodes, and you become a manager not a business owner. The creator learned this the hard way - large team, 12-14 hour days, Slack blowing up with problems, barely making profit.

Scalability

AI replaces most team members. One content manager can handle entire client roster using Fusion AI. Profit margins go from terrible (large team) to near-100% (AI + 1 person). Can take on unlimited clients without proportional hiring.

Best Quotes

It literally got to the point where every three clients I signed, I had to hire a new editor, script writer, or social media manager.
AI is literally able to handle 80% of the work for you. You need to have no prior experience.
Even though my revenue kept growing, it really felt like every extra client I signed, my business was just getting far more complex.
I really just knew I couldnt keep running my agency like this. I didnt want to build one where I was chained to my laptop, barely making a profit.

Action Steps

  • Use AI tools for content fulfillment (scripting, editing, ideation) to dramatically reduce team size and increase margins
  • Start with personal brand content to attract agency clients - document the journey publicly
  • Price at monthly retainers not one-off payments - recurring revenue is the path to sustainable business
  • Keep team minimal (1 content manager + AI) rather than scaling headcount with client growth

Full Description

Two specific AI agents generating $85K/month. Agent 1: Outbound Speed-to-Lead Agent - connects to CRM, calls new form submissions within 20 seconds, qualifies leads, books appointments. Replaces employees waiting to dial leads. Agent 2: Internal Quoting Agent - chatbot connecting to part suppliers, applying labor rates/markup/fees/gas costs, generating accurate quotes in seconds instead of 10-15 minutes manually. Live demo shown for mobile mechanic: employee inputs vehicle model, describes issue, gets instant quote with parts, markup, labor, fees.

Pain Point

Speed-to-Lead: businesses lose customers because employees take 20-40 minutes to call back. If not contacted within 5 minutes, lead calls next business. Quoting: owners spend 2-3 hours daily on free quotes (20-50/day at 10-15 min each).

Pricing Justification

Speed-to-Lead: employee costs 5% commission ($4-5K/month) + bad speed-to-lead + training time. Agent costs $2-3K, calls in 20 seconds, scales. Quoting: saves 2-3 hours daily of owner highest-leverage time. 3 hours/day reduced to 5 minutes/day.

Delivery Process

Speed-to-Lead: 1. Connect to client CRM. 2. Set trigger for new form submissions. 3. Agent calls within 20 seconds. 4. Qualifies based on knowledge base. 5. Books appointment. Quoting: 1. Connect to parts supplier API. 2. Get SOPs (labor rates, markup, fees, gas). 3. Train knowledge base. 4. Build internal chatbot. 5. Employee inputs vehicle model, selects exact model, describes issue, gets instant quote. 6. Upsell: external customer-facing chatbot.

Tools Stack

CRM integration, AI voice calling platform, Parts supplier API connections, Internal chatbot builder, Knowledge base training tools. Specific platforms not named - developer team handles technical choices.

Client Acquisition

Partner Model: Partner with marketing agencies who have 20-30 clients with high lead volume. Offer 20-30% commission per referral ($2-3K per $10-15K deal). Stack 5-10 agency partners. Also paid ads ($10K/month).

Outreach Script

Speed-to-Lead: Your show-up rate is only 50% because you get to leads 20-30 minutes late. You spend $5-6K on this employee who has bad speed-to-lead. This agent scales with your business, fixes your speed-to-lead, and costs less. Quoting: What would you do with 2-3 extra hours daily if you were not sending free quotes?

Sales Process

1. Partner with marketing agencies (20-30% commission). 2. Agency refers clients. 3. Discovery call focused on pain. 4. Never sell features, sell pain. 5. Show ROI math vs employee costs. 6. Close on monthly or hybrid. 7. Hand off to developers. 8. Move to next sales call.

Objection Handling

Already have someone: They cost 5% commission, have terrible speed-to-lead, need constant retraining. Do not need AI receptionist: This is not inbound receptionist (saturated), this is outbound speed-to-lead. Too expensive upfront: Switch to monthly recurring, compare to employee cost.

Contrarian Insight

Inbound AI receptionists are saturated - go opposite with outbound agents. If everyone on Instagram posts about Claude systems, that route will not make money. Never sell on features, sell on pain. 100% profit margin doing everything yourself makes LESS money than 75% with a team (2 clients/month vs 10). The quoting agent (internal, not customer-facing) is top seller.

Mistake Warning

Doing everything yourself limits to 2 clients/month. Selling inbound receptionists in saturated market. Selling on features instead of pain. Following where market is headed instead of going opposite.

Scalability

Partner model with marketing agencies -> First clients via referral commissions -> Hire US developers for 20% -> Owner focuses 100% on sales -> 5 speed-to-lead clients = $10K MRR -> 50 clients = $1M+ recurring -> Add quoting agent upsells at $12-20K -> Hire more developers as volume grows -> $85K+/month.

Best Quotes

It is 99% dominated by technical people who are really good on the back end but cannot sell.
If you can only take on two clients a month at 10K versus me taking on 10, that is how I have $80-100K months.
I get zero dopamine from sitting in back-end systems. I am not good at it.
Wherever the market is headed, head the other way.

Action Steps

  • Build an outbound speed-to-lead agent demo that calls within 20 seconds
  • Identify 5-10 marketing agencies and pitch the partner model at 20-30% commission
  • Find and vet 2-3 US-based AI developers for 20% of deal revenue
  • Build a quoting agent demo for mobile mechanics to show live in sales calls
  • Structure speed-to-lead deals as monthly recurring $2-3K to build predictable revenue

Build a Profitable Micro SaaS Business with AI in 		Micro-SaaS Tutorial on building micro SaaS products using Base44, an AI app builder. Micro Non-technical entrepreneurs, aspiring SaaS founders, people N/A - teaches pricing micro SaaS at $19/month as example $19/month example pricing. Funnel math: 10,000 visitors → 1,500 trials (15%) → 300 active (20%) → 150 paying (50%) = $2,850/month Examples: Bank Statement Converter $16K/month Audience-first approach: build 50+ engaged followe

Full Description

Tutorial on building micro SaaS products using Base44, an AI app builder. Micro SaaS = small, focused software solving one clear problem for one specific niche. Not trying to build the next billion-dollar unicorn. Examples: Bank Statement Converter ($16K/month), Screenshot One ($12K/month), Gift My Book (7-figure ARR). Framework covers idea validation through audience building, acute pain point identification, building minimal solution, generating word of mouth, and reinvesting in growth. Includes market gap heat map for finding underserved niches.

Pain Point

Most people cant build SaaS because they cant code and cant afford developers. Even with AI, most vibe-coded products get stuck at $10 MRR because the core idea is wrong, not the execution. The hardest part isnt building anymore - its choosing the right problem.

Pricing Justification

People dont pay for beautiful dashboards - they pay for relief. Save time, reduce mistakes, or make money easier to manage.

Delivery Process

1. Build audience first (50 engaged people enough). 2. Identify acute pain points from audience (not nice-to-have, need-this-fixed-NOW problems). 3. Build minimal solution - one job, one wow moment. 4. Generate word of mouth (one-click invites, shareable results). 5. Reinvest in audience growth with testimonials and proof.

Tools Stack

Base44 (AI app builder - primary, builds full SaaS from plain English descriptions), handles authentication, databases, email flows, payment integrations automatically. No coding required.

Client Acquisition

Audience-first approach: build 50+ engaged followers on X threads, LinkedIn, Reddit, Discord, or newsletter. Share insights, talk about problems. Audience tells you what to build through their complaints and frustrations.

Outreach Script

N/A - audience-driven inbound model

Sales Process

1. Prospect searches Google for solution to specific problem. 2. Lands on your tool page with clear promise. 3. Tries it - experiences wow moment within minutes. 4. Low friction trial → paid conversion. 5. Word of mouth spreads tool to others.

Objection Handling

People will happily compliment your idea but compliments dont build businesses - payments do. People tell the truth with their wallets. Test with payment, not praise.

Contrarian Insight

Ideas dont win - markets win. A genius idea in a weak market struggles. A simple idea in the right market prints. Large SaaS companies focus on massive industries, leaving smaller specific niches underserved. Build for overlooked groups where competition drops and willingness to pay goes up, especially in industries that look boring.

Mistake Warning

Picking the right idea in the wrong niche, or building before listening. Most beginners think the first step is building - its not. You win by listening first. Building without signal is just guessing, and guessing is expensive.

Scalability

Flywheel: audience → feedback → better features → better results → more word of mouth → more audience. Each cycle spins faster. Can reach $10K-$50K/month in right niche with focused funnel.

Best Quotes

Ideas dont win. Markets win. A genius idea in a weak market struggles. A simple idea in the right market prints.
You dont win by building first, you win by listening first. Building without signal is just guessing. Guessing is expensive.
People dont pay for beautiful dashboards, they pay for relief.
People will happily compliment your idea. But compliments dont build businesses. Payments do. People tell the truth with their wallets.

Action Steps

  • Use Base44 to build and launch a micro SaaS in a weekend - describe the tool in plain English and iterate
  • Start with 50 engaged people in a niche community, listen to their pain points, then build for their specific need
  • Target boring overlooked industries where competition is low and willingness to pay is high
  • Validate with payments not praise - charge from day one to test real demand

Health Varies by project - cost-saving or revenue-uplift based Retainer for ongoing management after initial build Scaled multiple agencies to $160K/month combi Four methods: 1) Upwork (highest conversion, least

Full Description

Nick Saraev's step-by-step playbook for AI consulting from $0 to $25K/month. Five pillars: Marketing, Sales, Onboarding, Fulfillment, Retention. Four marketing methods ranked: platform sales (Upwork), cold email, communities, cold DMs. Sales structure: rapport, schedule, discovery, solutions, investment. Scaled multiple agencies to $160K/month combined. Provides free templates, scripts, and workflows.

Pain Point

Businesses have money for AI but don't know how to implement it. Need specific, measurable results not vague promises.

Pricing Justification

Helped supplement company add $32K revenue in one month. Value-based: charge based on dollars saved or revenue generated, not hours worked.

Delivery Process

1. Marketing: Upwork proposals, cold email, community presence, cold DMs 2. Sales: rapport > set schedule > discovery > solutions > investment > proposal 3. Onboarding: structured intake process 4. Fulfillment: build and deploy automations 5. Retention: ongoing optimization and expansion

Tools Stack

Upwork (platform sales), Instantly (cold email), LinkedIn/Instagram/X (cold DMs), Maker School (community). Cold email infrastructure for scale.

Client Acquisition

Four methods: 1) Upwork (highest conversion, least scalable) 2) Cold email (most scalable, highest barrier) 3) Communities (slow but relationship-rich) 4) Cold DMs (high time, high potential)

Outreach Script

Cold DM example: 'Hey Sarah, I've been seeing XYZ Wellness everywhere recently. Huge work. I help health companies automate their onboarding and reduce churn with a $15,000 a month minimum guarantee. Just helped a supplement company add 32K in revenue in one month. Can I show you how I do the same for you? No strings.'

Sales Process

1. Build rapport (get them to smile) 2. Set the schedule ('Here's how these calls usually go...') 3. Discovery ('Why did you decide to book this call?' - highest ROI question ever) 4. Solutions (match their pain to your offer) 5. Investment (present pricing) 6. Send proposal

Objection Handling

Not detailed in pricing portion. Discovery-based selling: let client give you all ammunition through questions. Ask 'Why did you book this call?' to understand their motivation. Frame call agenda upfront to take control.

Contrarian Insight

Upwork is where to START - skip to top of buying ladder where prospects already have money in hand. 'Why did you decide to book the call?' is probably the highest ROI question ever and basically nobody asks it. First cold email campaign will be your worst - have runway to persist. Communities are like fishing in Runescape - slow start, very valuable at high level. Simple is NOT easy.

Mistake Warning

Spending time on anything other than lead generation at $0 revenue. Procrastinating on marketing. First cold email campaign being your worst and giving up. Not having runway for cold email experimentation. Being too formal in cold DMs.

Scalability

Upwork first gigs -> Cold email infrastructure -> Community authority -> Cold DMs -> All four channels simultaneously -> Scale to $25K+/month

Best Quotes

If you're at zero in revenue and spending any time on anything not directly generating leads, you are wasting money
Sales today is not about tricking people. It is about uncovering their pain
Why did you decide to book the call? Probably the highest ROI question ever and basically nobody asks it
Your first campaign is probably going to be your worst

Action Steps

  • Set up Upwork profile with custom CV and video proposal template
  • Write one cold email script following: personalization, value prop, niche, goal, case study, cliffhanger, CTA
  • Join 2-3 communities and post value content 3x/week
  • Practice the 5-step sales structure on your next call
  • Send 10 cold DMs on LinkedIn this week with the Sarah template

AI Customer Support Agent in n8n		 Automation Bart Slodyczka builds a complete AI customer support agent in n8n that integrate E-commerce businesses using Zendesk, Gorgeous, or Freshdesk Workflow template available on Gumroad (price not specified). Setup time: ~10 minutes. Agency model: ongoing retainer for maintenance and optimization Not specified in transcript YouTube tutorials, Gumroad template sales, agency

Full Description

Bart Slodyczka builds a complete AI customer support agent in n8n that integrates with Zendesk (also works with Gorgeous/Freshdesk). The system pulls tickets, generates AI responses (as internal notes or direct replies), logs everything to Google Sheets, and auto-generates FAQs from solved tickets. Uses Perplexity API restricted to client website instead of building a RAG database - eliminates double-handling of information.

Pain Point

Customer support teams overwhelmed with ticket volume. Need co-pilot to draft responses. Knowledge scattered across specialized human agents, Slack, YouTube videos. No centralized FAQ system. Manual response drafting is slow and inconsistent.

Pricing Justification

Eliminates or reduces need for multiple support agents. Consistent response quality. 24/7 availability. Auto-generated FAQs reduce future ticket volume.

Delivery Process

1. Create Zendesk webhook pointing to n8n 2. Create Zendesk trigger for new/updated tickets 3. n8n receives ticket ID via webhook 4. Two API calls: get ticket info + get all comments 5. Route: open tickets to response agent, solved tickets to FAQ generator 6. AI generates response using Perplexity API (restricted to client website) 7. Post response back to Zendesk (internal note or public reply) 8. Log everything to Google Sheets 9. Generate FAQs from solved tickets weekly

Tools Stack

n8n (workflow automation), Zendesk/Gorgeous/Freshdesk (CRM), Perplexity API (AI search restricted to client domain - replaces RAG/Pinecone), Google Sheets (logging and FAQ storage), OpenAI (response generation)

Client Acquisition

YouTube tutorials, Gumroad template sales, agency service offering

Sales Process

Not detailed - tutorial-focused content

Objection Handling

Safety concern: start with internal notes (co-pilot mode) before enabling direct customer replies. Accuracy: Perplexity API restricted to client website ensures responses based on actual product info.

Contrarian Insight

Don't build a RAG database with Pinecone - it's double-handling information that already exists on the client's website. Instead, use Perplexity API restricted to the website domain for live AI-powered search. Start with internal notes not direct replies - much safer. Use Google Sheets for logging every interaction instead of digging through the ticketing system. Auto-generate FAQs from solved tickets to build knowledge base organically.

Mistake Warning

Sending AI responses directly to customers before validating accuracy. Not logging interactions to a separate Google Sheet for easy review. Building RAG databases when the information already exists on the website. Not using different response styles for different channels (email vs SMS).

Scalability

Build template -> Sell on Gumroad -> Offer done-for-you setup -> Add ongoing monitoring retainer -> Expand to multiple CRM platforms -> Scale agency

Best Quotes

I'm not building a RAG database. I'm not using Pinecone. A lot of people have websites with heaps of pages and all the product information is on the website
We're using the Perplexity API search and restricting domains directly to the website
Initially I would just suggest responding back with internal notes because it's a lot safer
One thing I find is it's really good to build a Google Sheet where you can have every single interaction logged

Action Steps

  • Set up n8n with Zendesk webhook integration
  • Configure Perplexity API restricted to one client domain
  • Build the two-route workflow: responses for open tickets, FAQs for solved
  • Create Google Sheet logging template for all AI interactions
  • Start with internal notes only - review accuracy for 1 week before enabling direct replies

This video is a consumer-side critique of companies replacing human customer service representatives with AI chatbots. The creator (Amanda from Swell Entertainment) argues that AI chatbots fundamentally misunderstand the customer service role, fail at de-escalation, cannot make intuitive leaps, and create longer resolution times for simple problems. She frames it as companies treating consumers as obstacles between them and their money. Not an offer video - this is editorial commentary on the AI customer service trend.

Pain Point

AI chatbots are dumb, cannot understand nuanced problems, create roadblocks to reaching human agents, and waste customer time on issues that a human could solve in 5 minutes

Pricing Justification

N/A

Client Acquisition

N/A

Sales Process

N/A

Objection Handling

N/A

Contrarian Insight

Companies are outsourcing customer service to AI not because it is better but because they see consumers as obstacles to profit. The consumer is treated as the enemy. AI customer service is a fundamental misunderstanding of business - it trades short-term cost savings for massive long-term customer resentment.

Mistake Warning

Companies assuming simple customer service problems can be handled by AI chatbots - what appears simple actually requires human intuitive leaps and critical thinking that AI cannot replicate. The thin line between dumbest humans and smartest bears applies to customer service.

Scalability

N/A

Best Quotes

Your customer service chatbot is dumb and you should fire them.
It seems that a lot of things that companies do, it almost seems like they are irritated that they have to go through you, the consumer, to get to your money.
The same rules apply to customer service as applies to trash cans in national parks. There is a thin line between the dumbest humans and the smartest bears.
A human can make certain intuitive leaps and do a little bit of critical thinking that you dont realize how much that assists in the customer service role.

Action Steps

  • Use this video as market research on consumer sentiment - the anti-AI-chatbot sentiment is a selling point FOR well-built AI agents that actually work and can escalate to humans
  • When pitching AI receptionist services, address the objection that AI customer service is hated by consumers by showing how your solution differs from dumb chatbots
  • Position AI voice agents as solving missed calls (not replacing existing human service) to avoid the backlash described in this video

Not primary model - sold as owned asset, not monthly fee. 15 million total over ~3 years. 500K/month by Meta ads to opt-in, AI WhatsApp qualifier books ca

Full Description

Modular AI system converting leads into booked appointments. Combines AI voice agents (5 min response), AI WhatsApp/SMS setters (qualify, educate, book), CRM automation on GoHighLevel. Modular: separate agents for qualification, training, booking, follow-up. Sold as one-time 9.5-15K infrastructure asset. Built once, replicated across vertical.

Pain Point

MIT study: 5 min vs 30 min contact = 100x qualification drop. Human setters cost 25-30K/month, are slow and inconsistent. Revenue lost from no-shows and slow response.

Pricing Justification

25-30K/month on setters vs 15K once = saves 300K/year. Tool is commodity. 15K buys research intelligence. MIT: 5-min vs 30-min = 100x qualification.

Delivery Process

1. Pick vertical. 2. Deep research: problems, avatars, bottlenecks. 3. Position as growth infrastructure. 4. Build modular system on GHL. 5. Integrate AI voice for 5-min response. 6. Integrate AI WhatsApp/SMS setter. 7. Customize prompts with niche context. 8. Vary response delays (30s-1min). 9. Deploy and monitor. 10. Replicate (plug and play).

Tools Stack

GoHighLevel CRM: workflows, pipelines, prompt-based AI. Voice AI: best available provider. WhatsApp Business API. Meta Ads (800-2K to start). All commodities 20-200/month.

Client Acquisition

Meta ads to opt-in, AI WhatsApp qualifier books calls. Personalized Loom videos showing prospect problems. Student spent 800 on ads, closed 15K client.

Outreach Script

Research-first video showing market problems. WhatsApp flow: Thank you for opting in -> qualify business/audience/methods/challenge -> send free training -> book call.

Sales Process

1. Meta ads to niche audience. 2. AI WhatsApp qualifies. 3. AI sends educational content. 4. AI books prospect. 5. Prospect arrives pre-sold. 6. Close at 9.5-15K, 50% upfront. 7. Replicate.

Objection Handling

Not buying chatbot (20/month commodity). Buying intelligence for YOUR market. 25-30K/month setters vs 15K once = 300K/year savings.

Contrarian Insight

STOP FOCUSING ON AI TOOLS. n8n workflow skills worthless - million people watched same tutorial. Market understanding matters. Starting business from tech excitement is worst thing. Custom building = slavery disguised as entrepreneurship. Endgame: own intelligence, rent it out via AI platforms.

Mistake Warning

Custom solutions per client with no niche. Caps income. Student made 21K then lost to chargebacks - wrong market, no research. Came back with 800, deep dental research, hit 50K/month.

Scalability

0-1: ONE vertical, deep research, build once. 1-5: Replicate in vertical. 5-20: 25-45 clients/month. 20-50+: Own intelligence, rent via platforms. Service business = stepping stone. 12-month window.

Best Quotes

You will not make money by focusing on the tools and systems or AI in general.
People want to solve their problems with AI. If you dont understand their problems, youre not going to make money.
YouTube videos teaching you to build workflows is the thing that will kill you in business.
The tool itself is a commodity. How to build it to drive revenue - thats the unique part.

Action Steps

  • Pick ONE vertical and do 2-3 days deep research BEFORE building anything
  • Build modular AI system on GoHighLevel: separate agents for qualification, education, booking, follow-up
  • Price at 9,500-15,000 as one-time infrastructure asset - position against 25-30K/month setter costs
  • Use Meta ads (800-2K) to drive leads into your own AI WhatsApp qualifier
  • Study Hormozi momentum formula applied to AI: serve x pricing x delivery x acquisition x trend

Using Manus AI to Build an AI Agency in 2026		 Lead Gen Building an AI agency that offers lead generation through Meta ads plus AI voice HVAC, plumbing, roofing, solar (home services), legal servic $5,000 upfront (Manus AI suggested $3.5K, creator recommends $5K, can charge up to $10K) $2,500/month after initial 3-month commitment Agency scaling ad spend to $500-$1,000/day. H Paid ads for own agency (Facebook/Instagram). Crea

Full Description

Building an AI agency that offers lead generation through Meta ads plus AI voice callers to book appointments. Uses Manus AI (deep research agent with its own computer) to find niches, build pricing models, and research competitors. Uses ArcAds for AI-generated video ads ($7/video). Uses GoHighLevel as CRM backend. The creator runs a high-ticket medical treatment agency currently scaling ad spend to $500-1,000/day. Teaches using paid ads (not cold outreach) as the primary client acquisition method.

Pain Point

80% of local businesses have no clue how to implement AI but see it on the news daily and know they need it. They need lead generation and appointment setting but cant do it themselves.

Pricing Justification

Manus AI generates data-backed pricing with average cost per lead and average lead value per niche. HVAC example: cost per lead data directly shows ROI to prospects.

Delivery Process

1. Use Manus AI to research best niches (generates full Google doc with cost per lead, lead value data). 2. Build pricing model with Manus AI help. 3. Set up GoHighLevel CRM backend. 4. Create AI video ads with ArcAds ($7/video, female actors perform better). 5. Run Meta ads for clients. 6. Deploy Retail AI voice callers to call and book leads into appointments. 7. Use paid ads for own client acquisition.

Tools Stack

Manus AI ($20/month - deep research agent with own computer, better than ChatGPT for research), ArcAds.ai (AI video ad generation, $7/video, lip-synced), GoHighLevel (CRM, automation backend), Retail AI (voice AI callers), Meta/Facebook/Instagram ads platform, Claude/ChatGPT (ad script generation). Ideogram mentioned for image ads.

Client Acquisition

Paid ads for own agency (Facebook/Instagram). Creator explicitly says cold outreach, email blasts, SMS blasts, cold calling are lies sold by YouTube gurus. Every big agency owner uses paid ads because its almost automated - inbound leads book calls and want your service.

Outreach Script

N/A - uses paid ads not outreach. For client ads, uses ChatGPT/Claude to generate 35-45 second video scripts, then ArcAds generates the video.

Sales Process

1. Run paid ads for own agency. 2. Inbound prospects book sales calls. 3. Close on $5K upfront + $2.5K/month × 3 months. 4. Deliver lead gen + AI calling. 5. Upsell additional services.

Objection Handling

Addresses AI ads look fake concern: most people on social media have their brains turned off and dont notice. Even those who do notice still engage. Shows real examples of AI-generated video ads performing well.

Contrarian Insight

People on YouTube who claim cold outreach, email blasts, and SMS blasts work for getting agency clients are lying. Every big agency owner uses paid ads. Its almost automated - inbound people already interested book calls. Also: Manus AI is way better than ChatGPT for deep research because it has its own computer and can browse real websites live.

Mistake Warning

Being broad instead of being a master of one niche. If youre working with roofing, med spa, law firms, and accounting firms, youre essentially running four different businesses of fulfillment. Stick with one niche for 3-6 months minimum. Dont niche-hop - youre just restarting your business each time.

Scalability

Master one niche → duplicate service delivery across clients in same vertical. Use paid ads for predictable client acquisition. AI handles ad creation ($7/video) and lead calling (Retail AI). Scale ad spend as results prove out.

Best Quotes

80% of local businesses have no clue how to implement AI but they see it on the news every single day and they need to be a part of it.
People on YouTube who claim that outreach and email blasts and cold calling work for getting clients are lying to you. Setting up paid ads is what every big agency owner does.
You want to be a master of one, not average at all. If youre working with roofing, med spa, law firms, and accounting, youre doing four different businesses.
Manus AI is way better than ChatGPT, better than Claude, better than everything Ive seen when it comes to doing deep research.

Action Steps

  • Use Manus AI ($20/month) for niche research with data-backed cost-per-lead and lead value analysis
  • Create AI video ads with ArcAds at $7/video - use female actors for better performance
  • Set up GoHighLevel as CRM backend and Retail AI for voice calling
  • Run paid ads for your own agency instead of cold outreach - every successful agency owner does this

AI Agents that Work		 Consulting Greg Isenberg and Remy Gasill explain AI agents in beginner-friendly terms. Core Beginners wanting to understand and use AI agents. Founders N/A - educational content N/A Not personal revenue claims. Demonstrates age Suggested: mass cold email with pre-built websites

Full Description

Greg Isenberg and Remy Gasill explain AI agents in beginner-friendly terms. Core concept: chat is question-to-answer, agents are goal-to-result. Agents use an observe-think-act loop until task is complete. Four components: LLM brain, loop mechanism, tools, and context. Agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Anti-Gravity, OpenClaw) are like different cars - learn to drive once, use any harness. Demo builds portfolio websites across three platforms simultaneously.

Pain Point

AI landscape moving from chat to agents and most people getting left behind. Founders using agents are 10-20x more productive. Confusion about what agents actually are and how they work.

Pricing Justification

10-20x productivity gain from using agents vs chat. Mass cold email pre-built websites for $250 each - nearly zero marginal cost once system is built.

Delivery Process

1. Understand agent loop (observe-think-act) 2. Choose an agent harness (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) 3. Set up workspace/folder structure 4. Connect tools via MCPs 5. Load context (system prompts, files) 6. Give goal-oriented prompts 7. Let agent loop until task complete 8. Review and iterate

Tools Stack

Claude Code (best loop visibility), Codex (OpenAI), Anti-Gravity (Google/Gemini), OpenClaw (wild west). MCPs for tool connections (Perplexity for research). Local folder-based project structure.

Client Acquisition

Suggested: mass cold email with pre-built websites as lead magnet

Outreach Script

Suggested cold email: 'Hey, I built you this website. If you want it, it's $250.' Mass cold email approach with off-the-shelf pre-made websites.

Sales Process

1. Scrape businesses without websites 2. Agent builds portfolio site automatically 3. Cold email with demo link 4. Prospect reviews free preview 5. Pay $250 to own it 6. Upsell ongoing services

Objection Handling

Not detailed in transcript

Contrarian Insight

Chat is question-to-answer. Agent is goal-to-result. This is the key mindset shift. Agent harnesses are like cars - learn to drive once and you can use any of them. The concepts transfer across all platforms. Security is about scoping access, not avoiding agents. Pre-making websites for businesses and cold emailing them is a blue ocean opportunity.

Mistake Warning

Staying in chat mode when agents are 10-20x more productive. Thinking you need to learn every agent platform (learn concepts once, apply anywhere). Not understanding the observe-think-act loop. Giving agents too much access without scoping permissions.

Scalability

Learn agent concepts -> Pick one harness -> Build simple agents -> Automate repeatable tasks -> Offer agent-built deliverables to businesses -> Scale via automation

Best Quotes

Chat model is question to answer, agent is goal to result
Founders and employees utilizing agents are 10 to 20 times more productive
Agent harnesses are like different cars. Once you know how to drive, you can jump in any of them
Pre-making websites for companies and cold emailing - Hey I built you this website, if you want it its $250

Action Steps

  • Install Claude Code or Codex and run your first agent task
  • Build a simple portfolio website using an agent to understand the loop
  • Connect one external tool via MCP (like Perplexity for research)
  • Identify a repeatable task in your business that an agent could handle
  • Test the cold email website approach with 10 local businesses

Businesses missing leads, poor follow-up, unoptimized sales scripts, no-show appointments

Pricing Justification

Pre-call content consumption builds trust before price discussion. 7 hours of content consumption needed for buying decision.

Delivery Process

On call: intro -> discovery -> conversion frame -> high-level overview pitch 5. Present 3-pillar system on Lucid Chart 6. Close with utility belt ROI calculations

Tools Stack

Sendinflow AI (AI calling platform), GoHighLevel (CRM, automations, SMS), Lucid Chart (pitch visuals), AI actors for ad creation

Client Acquisition

Not detailed - focus is on closing booked calls

Pre-call video consumption + post-booking SMS: broken into multiple messages 6-12 seconds apart to look human

Sales Process

1. Pre-call video consumption 2. Post-booking automation sequence 3. Intro - check pre-call video watched 4. Discovery - where are you now, where going, now or later, need help? 5. Conversion frame - yes/no/think about it anchor 6. High-level overview pitch on Lucid Chart 7. Utility belt ROI calculations 8. Close

Objection Handling

Kill zombies early - ask for all questions upfront. Conversion frame anchors them to yes/no decision on the call. Utility belt has gadgets for every objection with ROI math.

Contrarian Insight

If they didnt watch pre-call content, dont take the sales call. Reschedule until they consume content. Confused buyers dont buy - never open a single software on the call.

Mistake Warning

Most AI agencies confuse prospects by showing complex software on sales calls. Keep pitch to simple 3-pillar visual. Never open software during pitch.

Scalability

Pre-call content does the heavy lifting. By the time they get on call, youre a glorified cashier. Scale by improving pre-call content and automating more of the nurture.

Best Quotes

Last month I did $124,000 on this payment processor alone
On average it takes 7 hours of content consumption for a buyer to make their educated decision
If you confuse people theyre not going to buy. Confused buyers dont buy
By the time they hop on the sales call they already know who you are what you sell

Pain Point

Pricing by the hour trains clients to see you as expensive labor. Creates adversarial relationship where clients micromanage time instead of valuing outcomes.

Pricing Justification

You keep 80-90% of value, I take 10-20% for making it happen. $8K doesnt seem expensive against $240K annual revenue.

Delivery Process

1. Identify measurable outcome 2. Quantify impact in dollars 3. Charge 10-20% of first year value 4. Lead with diagnosis not price 5. Itemize retainer value (monitoring, optimization, reports, support) 6. Build one case study, double price each project

Not provided directly - teaches diagnostic conversation approach

Scalability

Action Steps

  • Build one case study with before/after metrics
  • Use the 20% rule on your next proposal
  • Lead sales conversations with diagnosis not price
  • Create hybrid offers combining setup fee plus monthly retainer

Build an AI-powered missed call text back system inside GoHighLevel that automatically texts leads who call a business and get no answer. Pain Point

57% of sales goes to whoever responds first (data-backed). Most small businesses let calls go to voicemail and hope people call back - they don't. Static one-text auto-replies don't engage or convert. Business owners are losing jobs and revenue every time they miss a call.

If the system books even one extra job per month for a service business, it pays for itself many times over. 90-day money-back guarantee eliminates risk.

Use Claude/ChatGPT to generate industry-specific AI personality and instructions. 9. Set bot parameters: wait 24 hours for reply, SMS channel, max 5 responses, 35-second delay between responses. 10. Remove quotation marks from question field (critical detail). 11. Add branching conditions: Booked (provided service need + address + preferred day), Emergency (urgent situation), Unqualified (outside area or irrelevant). 12. Set up SMS notifications for each branch. 13. Publish and save. 14. Duplicate workflow for dog fooding client acquisition.

When business owners call back, GHL triggers AI text-back that sells them the service.

Outreach Script

Ringless voicemail: 'Hey, this is Chris Kerner. I'm here in Dallas, Texas, and I'm looking for a tree trimming business. So, please give me a call back. Thanks.' AI sales text: 'Hey, I know this is random, but I'm using a missed call text back on you right now that will have a full conversation with you with AI. It feels real, doesn't it? It is $500 a month, but if it doesn't pay for itself in the first 90 days, then I'll give you all your money back. Can we hop on a call so I can explain? It'll only take a minute.'

Sales Process

1. Scrape phone numbers for target business type via Outscraper. 2. Record vague 10-second ringless voicemail. 3. Send RVM drops to entire list. 4. AI text-back system engages callers automatically. 5. AI qualifies interest (hot lead vs unqualified). 6. Business owner gets SMS with lead name and phone for hot leads. 7. Human follows up to close on a call.

Objection Handling

Price objection built into AI: '$500/month but if it doesn't pay for itself in the first 90 days, then it's free.' Risk-reversal close automated in the sales conversation.

Contrarian Insight

Dog fooding - use the exact same AI system you're selling to FIND and CLOSE clients. Every business has two functions: find customers and fulfill those customers. Leaving quotation marks in the AI question field (embarrassing when sent). Setting delay between AI responses too low (10 seconds feels robotic - use 35 seconds). Not adding branching conditions for emergency/unqualified which wastes time.

Copy-paste workflow for every new client - just swap business-specific info. 33 million small business owners as addressable market. Dog fooding workflow generates leads passively through ringless voicemail drops. Community (Playmakers at playmakersai.com) for support.

Full Description

Five specific simple automations: (1) Search Intent Scraping - scrapes LinkedIn job postings, finds decision-makers via AnyMailFinder, researches them with Perplexity, generates custom icebreakers, adds to Instantly cold email sequences. (2) AI Podcast Repurposing Engine - transcribes podcasts, extracts 10 best points, generates platform-specific social posts with images, auto-publishes on schedule. (3) Automatic Invoice Collection/Follow-up - monitors unpaid invoices and automates follow-up. (4-5) Additional automations not fully detailed in first 15K chars. Built in Make.com and n8n.

Pain Point

Companies spend thousands hiring SDRs when AI can identify and outreach prospects automatically. Creators have long-form content but no time to repurpose. Huge money tied up in unpaid invoices for B2B businesses.

Pricing Justification

Simple systems generate substantial ROI. Invoice collection recovers thousands. Podcast repurposing replaces a social media manager. Search intent scraping replaces manual prospecting.

Delivery Process

System 1 (Search Intent): 1. Set LinkedIn job search URL. 2. Apify scrapes job postings. 3. Filter (website exists, not LinkedIn, under 150 employees). 4. Check Google Sheets for duplicates. 5. Add new companies to database. 6. GPT-4 mini filters for relevance. 7. AnyMailFinder finds decision-maker. 8. Perplexity researches prospect. 9. AI generates custom icebreaker. 10. Add to Instantly cold email campaign. System 2 (Podcast): 1. Input URL. 2. Apify YouTube Transcript Ninja extracts transcript. 3. AI identifies 10 engaging points. 4. Generate Instagram/LinkedIn/Facebook posts. 5. DALL-E generates images. 6. Store in Google Sheets by platform. 7. Schedule trigger publishes daily.

Tools Stack

Apify ($49+/month - LinkedIn scraper, YouTube Transcript Ninja), Make.com (invoice system), n8n (scraping and repurposing), Google Sheets (database), AnyMailFinder (email enrichment), Perplexity AI (web research), OpenAI GPT-4 mini (filtering, icebreakers, content), DALL-E (images), Instantly (cold email, swappable with SmartLead), Instagram/LinkedIn/Facebook Graph APIs (posting)

Client Acquisition

YouTube technical tutorials build authority. The search intent scraping system itself is a client acquisition tool.

Contrarian Insight

The systems that make money are NOT flashy chatbots or AI agents. They are boring, simple, straight-line automations. Complex agents on YouTube are overhyped. Simple systems close better because business owners can understand them.

Mistake Warning

Do not build complex AI agents when simple automations sell better. Do not overcomplicate things. A Google Sheet as a database works fine. The systems that actually make money are boring.

Scalability

Build 5 template automations -> Sell each for $1,500+ -> Stack clients -> Multiple automations per client -> Scale to $72K/month by systematizing delivery.

Best Quotes

These are not flashy chatbots. They are not AI agents. What they are are unsexy but very simple straight-line automations.
I sold systems just like this when I scaled my automation agency to $72,000 per month.
The systems that make money do not have to be these big complex scary-looking agents you see all over YouTube.
Usually it is the very simple systems that generate substantial ROIs because you can explain them to the business owner.

Full Description

Patrick Dang teaches building a one-person AI-powered business centered on personal brand and content creation. His framework: YouTube content drives attention into lead magnets, which capture emails, which feed into webinars or sales calls, which convert to paying clients. He uses Claude and Claude Design to build landing pages, lead magnets, and webinar pages. The defensible moat is personal brand - AI commoditizes products but not reputation. He offers free live training and paid coaching programs to teach this system.

Pain Point

People spend hours learning to build perfect products but cannot get their first customer. Distribution is the bottleneck - if nobody knows who you are, you will not make a dime. 86% of new businesses are one-person operations.

Pricing Justification

Client Sandy went from not knowing what Claude was to gaining 20,000+ subscribers from zero in 2 months and appearing on a podcast with 100,000+ views

Delivery Process

1. Choose what to sell (AI-powered service recommended) and who to sell it to. 2. Build content machine: YouTube → lead magnets → email → webinar/sales call → client. 3. Use Claude Design to build lead magnet landing pages and webinar pages. 4. Get results for clients, turn results into content, feed machine. 5. Rinse and repeat - content machine compounds.

Tools Stack

Claude AI (primary), Claude Design (for landing pages, lead magnets, webinar pages), Claude Co-work, Squarespace (sponsor mention). Camera + microphone + laptop + internet for content creation.

Client Acquisition

YouTube content creation driving attention into lead magnet funnels. Free live training as conversion event. Content machine: YouTube → lead magnet → email → webinar/sales call → client.

Outreach Script

N/A - inbound content-driven model, not outreach

Sales Process

1. Create YouTube content solving target audience problems. 2. Offer free lead magnet (e.g., Ikigai skill for finding business idea). 3. Capture emails. 4. Nurture via email. 5. Invite to webinar or sales call. 6. Convert to paying client. 7. Get results → create case study content → feed back into machine.

Objection Handling

Mountain of Cringe framework - acknowledges haters and fear of starting. Shows his own journey: $200 to his name, parents spare bedroom, wallpaper to fake a studio, credit card loans for equipment. Made first $1,000 within a month.

Contrarian Insight

Your audience is your moat, not your product. In the era of AI, anyone can copy your product in minutes with Claude. The only defensible moat is personal brand and distribution. Code and products are commodities - reputation is not. Naval Ravikant quote used.

Mistake Warning

Focusing on building and planning the perfect product instead of distribution. Even after watching hours of tutorials, most people cannot get their first customer because they neglect distribution.

Scalability

Content machine compounds: more content → more views → more leads → more clients → more results → more content. Client Sandy example shows the model scales through audience growth.

Best Quotes

The most important thing in building a one person business is distribution. You could be the best in the world at what you do, but if nobody knows who you are, you will not make a dime.
In the era of AI, its going to be extremely easy for anybody to copy another persons products and services. So if everybody can copy each other, the only real defensible moat is building a personal brand.
Your audience is your moat. Your email list is your moat. Your community is your moat and your reputation is your moat. Code and products are all commodities.
Im really just a glorified content creator. My job is to make the best content, teach people the stuff that I learned so they can do it too.

Action Steps

  • Use Claude Design to rapidly prototype landing pages and lead magnets instead of paying $1-2K for designers
  • Build content machine flywheel: YouTube → lead magnet → email → sales call → client → results → content
  • Start with personal brand and distribution before perfecting the product - distribution is the bottleneck not product quality
  • Use Ikigai framework to identify business idea at intersection of skills, passion, market need, and monetization

TK Kader / Unstoppable
3 Profitable AI SaaS Ideas to Build in 2026		 SaaS TK Kader shares 3 AI SaaS ideas using his Unstoppable Ideas framework (Who, Why, Idea 1: Salespeople, HR, recruiters, PR, legal professionals Free trial / freemium start $30/month starting, expandable to $99+/month with CRM integration and additional data sources Previous company ToutApp: backed by a16z, sol Product-led growth. Free trial → immediate value →

Full Description

TK Kader shares 3 AI SaaS ideas using his Unstoppable Ideas framework (Who, Why, What). Idea 1: Trained Negotiator - Chrome extension sitting inside Gmail that applies human psychology to read email threads and provides negotiation advice, draft responses, and insights on what the other party is really saying. Targets salespeople, HR, recruiters, PR, legal. Idea 2: Website Message Creator - helps founders constantly changing their website messaging by analyzing if their messaging resonates with target audience, combating AI-induced delusion where ChatGPT makes everything sound legit. Both priced at $30-99/month targeting commission-based roles.

Pain Point

Idea 1: People spend all day negotiating via email but manually copy-paste threads into Gemini for analysis - repetitive and inefficient. Idea 2: Founders are delusionally confident in messaging because ChatGPT validates everything. They need objective AI analysis of whether messaging actually resonates with their market.

Pricing Justification

People will pay for convenience AND expertise. Not every salesperson knows the right prompts. The custom alpha is specialized prompts plus workflow integration inside existing tools. If it helps them close one more deal, the ROI is obvious.

Delivery Process

1. Build Chrome extension for Gmail. 2. Apply trained negotiation prompts to email thread context. 3. Provide analysis of counterpartys position, unsaid cues, and recommended responses. 4. Integrate with CRM data for richer context. 5. Add chat interface for deeper conversation analysis.

Tools Stack

Chrome extension (primary delivery), Gmail integration, CRM integration (Salesforce, HubSpot), AI models for NLP analysis. Can expand to Outlook. Replit, Lovable, or GitHub for building.

Client Acquisition

Product-led growth. Free trial → immediate value → credit card. Target commission-based roles who are incentivized to invest in tools that increase earnings.

Sales Process

1. User installs Chrome extension. 2. Opens email thread in Gmail. 3. Trained Negotiator analyzes thread and provides insights. 4. User sees value immediately. 5. Converts to paid at $30/month.

Objection Handling

Why not just use ChatGPT/Gemini? Answer: People pay for convenience AND expertise. The specialized prompts and in-context workflow integration are the moat. Also connects to CRM data for richer analysis that manual prompting cant replicate.

Contrarian Insight

AI-induced delusion is a real problem. Founders get into long enough conversations with ChatGPT and everything it says seems totally legit, leading to delusional confidence in messaging that doesnt actually resonate with the market. The antidote is objective, data-driven messaging analysis.

Mistake Warning

The worst thing to do is waste months building the wrong product or building a product no one wants. Always validate the Who (ICP), Why (pain), and What (10x better solution) before building.

Scalability

Chrome extension → team licenses → enterprise. Start at $30/month individual → $99+/month with CRM integration → enterprise pricing for sales teams. Can expand from Gmail to Outlook and other platforms.

Best Quotes

Anytime theres copy and paste into Gemini and youre trying to prompt it the right way, theres an opportunity for a SaaS business.
People will pay for convenience, but more importantly, people will pay for expertise.
Theres this thing happening where you get into a long enough conversation with ChatGPT and anything it says to you just seems totally legit. You end up being completely delusional.
What makes for a great SaaS idea is not about vibe coding the product. Its the core kernel of the idea - whether it was a good idea in terms of the market youre going after.

Action Steps

  • Build a Trained Negotiator Chrome extension for Gmail that analyzes email threads and provides negotiation coaching
  • Target commission-based roles (sales, recruiting, PR) who are financially incentivized to pay for productivity tools
  • Start at $30/month and expand pricing with CRM integrations that provide richer context
  • Use the Who-Why-What framework to validate any SaaS idea before building

Full Description

Comprehensive breakdown of Alex Hormozis lead generation strategy across his $200M+ portfolio of 16 companies. Five philosophies: 1) Self-reinforcing system (customers → reviews/referrals → more customers), 2) Rule of reciprocity (give free value so people feel they owe you), 3) Extreme ownership (dont blame market), 4) Avoid linear growth (use automation/content not just grinding), 5) Three pillars (high quality leads + treat customers well + get reviews/referrals). Covers Core Four: warm outreach, cold outreach, content, paid ads. Includes verbatim script from Hormozi doing live warm outreach.

Pain Point

Relying only on grinding creates hamster wheel growth. No reviews/referral system means leaving money on table. Word of mouth is highest percentage of sales across any market but most businesses dont ask for reviews or referrals.

Pricing Justification

Hormozi gives away all courses and secrets for free → builds reciprocity → people buy whatever he offers because they feel they owe him.

Delivery Process

1. Start with warm outreach (call people you know). 2. Follow Hormozi script: introduction → ask about their life → ask if they have time for [your service] → ask if they know anyone else → offer free trial. 3. Track everything in CRM/Notion. 4. Build self-reinforcing system: deliver results → get reviews/referrals → more clients. 5. Add cold outreach, content, and paid ads as you scale.

Tools Stack

Notion (momentum operating system for tracking outreach and leads), Instantly (automated outbound email campaigns), CRM tools. Hormozi framework: Core Four (warm outreach, cold outreach, content, paid ads).

Client Acquisition

Hormozis Core Four: 1) Warm outreach (call people you know first), 2) Cold outreach, 3) Content creation, 4) Paid advertising. Start with warm outreach for immediate results.

Outreach Script

Hormozi verbatim warm outreach script: Hey whats up man, [ask about their life]. Quick question for you - is anyone [doing your service]? No? Got it. Do you know anybody else who also might not have [service]? What Im trying to do is Im looking for five or ten people to do my service for free just so I can show how good my service is. Ill text you with the details. The other folks you know, do you think you could do a three-way text intro with me?

Sales Process

1. Introduction (ask about their life). 2. Ask if they have the problem your service solves. 3. Ask for referrals (do you know anyone else?). 4. Offer free trial to build momentum. 5. Follow up and track in CRM. 6. Convert free trials to paid via demonstrated results.

Objection Handling

If nervous: follow a script. Hormozi provides exact word-for-word script. Free trial removes the money objection. Three-way text intro removes the I dont know anyone objection.

Contrarian Insight

You probably have gold sitting in your phone, Instagram followers, and LinkedIn connections right now. Most people rely on cold outreach when warm outreach can get a deal in minutes. Also: the harder I work the more my business grows is a hamster wheel - you need systems and automation, not just grinding. And: most people dont ask for reviews/referrals despite word of mouth being the highest percentage of sales.

Mistake Warning

Not building a self-reinforcing system. Just doing get the next deal, get the next deal without reviews/referrals/automation means youre always on a hamster wheel. Also: not tracking outreach in a CRM - spraying and praying without data means no learning.

Scalability

Warm outreach → free trials → results → reviews/referrals → self-reinforcing flywheel. Add cold outreach (Instantly email automation), content creation, and paid ads as momentum builds. Notion operating system tracks everything.

Best Quotes

The highest percentage of sales across any market come from word of mouth.
We want to create a system that is self-reinforcing that continues to grow and compound over time.
The rule of reciprocity: offer free stuff that others charge for so people feel like they owe you.
If youre not getting customers, dont blame the market. Point the finger at yourself.

Most AI content tutorials come from creators who only succeed because of high AI content demand, not because their system works in competitive niches.

340K subscribers and seven figures in sales from YouTube channel. Client attraction through demonstrated expertise and content quality.

Use Claude Skills for research (Content Market Intelligence skill scans Twitter, Reddit, forums, YouTube for trending topics). 4. Write script with Claude assistance but human judgment. 5. Film and edit. 6. Review analytics and iterate.

Claude (primary - chat and co-work modes), Claude Skills (MD files as specialized AI agents), Claude co-work (saves files, remembers context, can schedule tasks). Custom skills created: Content Market Intelligence, idea generation. Human editing and filming still required.

Client Acquisition

YouTube content → free training → high-ticket client conversion. Content quality is the acquisition mechanism.

Outreach Script

N/A - inbound content-driven model

Sales Process

1. Create high-quality YouTube content. 2. Offer free training. 3. Attract high-ticket clients through demonstrated expertise. 4. Content converts viewers to clients.

Objection Handling

Addresses but everyone says automate 90% with Claude: those creators only succeed because AI content has high demand. Take their system and apply it to any competitive niche - it wont work. The outputs matter, not the automation. Addresses AI will do everything: Claude is like Rocky from Project Hail Mary - super smart in some things, really dumb in others, still needs human judgment.

Contrarian Insight

Most Claude content automation tutorials are taught by creators who are not actually great content creators - they only pop off because of AI topic demand. If you took their automated system and applied it to any niche outside AI, they would get zero views. Do not automate things you cannot do manually first. If you cant write a YouTube script yourself, how will you judge if Claudes output is good? Check any gurus Instagram - if they get 2 likes per post, whats the point of automating something nobody watches?

Mistake Warning

Spending 80% of your time configuring Claude and APIs and terminals with no results to show. The whole point of content is to get clients. Also: dont try to automate 90% of your workflow on day one. Start small - even saving one hour per day is a game-changer because it stacks up. And dont create AI slop - ask yourself would you be proud to put this out?

Scalability

Content machine compounds: better positioning → better packaging → more views → more clients → more proof → better content. Claude Skills level up over time as you add more specialized MD files. One content engine serves multiple platforms (YouTube, Instagram, LinkedIn).

Best Quotes

All these creators are not actually great content creators. They started to pop off because of the popularity of AI. Take their machine and apply it to any other niche - it wont work.
Do not automate things you cannot do manually first. If you cant write a YouTube script, how are you going to have Claude automate it?
Packaging is 70-80% of success on YouTube. If nobody clicks, nobody watches.
Whatever process they do, look at the outputs. Go on their Instagram. If they get two likes, whats the point of automating something nobody watches?

Action Steps

  • Create custom Claude Skills (MD files) for your specific content niche - Content Market Intelligence, idea generation, script writing
  • Focus on packaging first (idea + thumbnail + title) before worrying about automation - its 70-80% of success
  • Only automate processes you can already do manually well - start with one hour saved per day
  • Judge AI content quality by asking: would I be proud to put this out? If not, dont publish it
