7-Figure Pricing for Automation		 Automation Nick Saraev breaks down 8 pricing methods for automation agencies: hourly, cost- SMBs needing automations (10 staff), enterprise companies (1 Cost-saving example: $10-15K one-time (25% of $50K annual savings). Revenue uplift: 10% of revenue generated. Ongoing maintenance retainers after initial build. Subscription models for recurring value. $100K+ in one month. Scaled agency to $72K/mo Upwork ($500K+ earned), cold outreach, community b

Full Description

Nick Saraev breaks down 8 pricing methods for automation agencies: hourly, cost-saving, revenue uplift, flat project fee, retainer, subscription, hybrid, and value-based. Made $100K+ in one month using make.com. Scaled agency to $72K/month. Each method has specific use cases, pros, and cons. No pricing method is perfect - best agencies constantly re-evaluate.

Pain Point

Pricing is the biggest and hardest moving part of automation. Beginners undercharge because they price on time not value. The time spent building doesn't reflect the value delivered.

Pricing Justification

Cost-saving: if you eliminate a $50K/year employee role, charge $12.5K (25%). Revenue uplift: if cold email system generates $X, charge 10% of that. Value-based: if 1% margin improvement on $100M company = $1M, charge accordingly.

Delivery Process

1. Consult with client to understand pain points 2. Identify cost savings or revenue opportunities 3. Propose value-based pricing 4. Build automation using make.com/n8n 5. Deploy and test 6. Transition to maintenance retainer 7. Re-evaluate pricing as relationship evolves

Tools Stack

make.com (primary automation platform), Zapier, n8n. No-code/low-code automation tools.

Client Acquisition

Upwork ($500K+ earned), cold outreach, community building (Maker School)

Sales Process

1. Discover client pain points 2. Quantify cost savings or revenue opportunity 3. Propose pricing as percentage of value 4. Build and deliver 5. Transition to retainer

Objection Handling

Client worried about cost escalation with hourly: switch to flat fee. Client questioning value: quantify in dollars saved or revenue generated. Uncertainty about scope: start with hourly discovery then transition to value-based.

Contrarian Insight

No pricing method is perfect. Hourly penalizes you for being good (work faster = make less). Cost-saving is harder to justify than revenue uplift because saving money feels less exciting than making money. You can never charge the full amount you save - max about half due to risk and uncertainty. The time you spend building does NOT reflect value delivered. Template-based systems can make you $10K+ in a few hours.

Mistake Warning

Sticking with hourly pricing past first few gigs. Not talking about money with prospects (the elephant in the room). Quoting way too much or way too little from lack of experience. Not re-evaluating pricing as you grow.

Scalability

Hourly gigs -> Cost-saving projects -> Revenue uplift deals -> Retainer + subscription hybrid -> Enterprise value-based pricing -> Multiple pricing models for different client tiers

Best Quotes

The time that you spend building a system does not accurately reflect the value that you bring to an organization
If you are really really good you are going to work much faster and make less money because of it
You can make 10,000 bucks in a few hours if you build it right
No pricing method is perfect

Action Steps

  • Audit current pricing: are you charging hourly? Plan transition to value-based
  • For next prospect: quantify their cost savings AND revenue opportunity in dollars
  • Create pricing templates for cost-saving and revenue uplift proposals
  • Practice talking about money in discovery calls
  • Build one templated automation you can deploy in hours and charge $5-10K for

Best service has broad market, clear measurable result, in-demand trend, scalable future. Agency model is king for low barrier entry, cash flow first, skill stacking. LTV must exceed 10K for paid acquisition scaling. Chatbot industry flagged as lacking scalable future.

Businesses terrified competitors will adopt AI first. Need measurable results not vanity metrics. Fear of the AI bloodbath - established businesses losing to 1-year-old AI-equipped competitors.

Pricing Justification

Revenue proximity rule: closer to revenue = more you can charge. Must have clear measurable result (not vanity metrics like engagement). 10K+ LTV enables paid acquisition scaling.

Delivery Process

1. Choose broad market service 2. Ensure clear measurable result 3. Tap in-demand AI trend 4. Verify scalable future 5. Get first 3-5 clients for case studies 6. Scale with monthly retainers 7. Add performance fees 8. Scale via paid acquisition once LTV > 10K

Not detailed in transcript

Contrarian Insight

Chatbot industry does NOT have a scalable future - be wary. SMMA (organic social media management) has poor measurable results leading to high churn. Revenue proximity rule from McKinsey: the closer your service is to directly generating revenue, the more you can charge and the stickier your clients. Skill stacking from running an agency makes every future business easier. Agency is gateway business, not end state.

Mistake Warning

Getting greedy with first clients instead of building case studies (proof > profit). Choosing a niche that is not measurable in revenue impact. Building in a vertical without scalable future (chatbots). Not ensuring LTV exceeds 10K before investing in paid acquisition. Ignoring the revenue proximity rule.

Scalability

Case study clients -> Monthly retainers $2-10K -> Performance fees -> LTV > 10K -> Paid acquisition -> $10-50K retainers -> Cash flow into other ventures

The closer you are in proximity to revenue, the more you can charge

  • Calculate your current client LTV - is it above 10K?

Full Description

An AI voice receptionist that answers calls 24/7 for local businesses, qualifies leads, collects contact info, and books appointments directly on the call. Built entirely inside GoHighLevel with voice AI, knowledge base web crawling, and calendar integration. Setup takes 1-2 hours per client. Positioned as a missed revenue recovery system not software.

Pain Point

62% of calls to local businesses go unanswered. 78% of buyers go with the FIRST business that responds. A plumber found 8 out of 12 missed callers had already hired someone else that same day. HVAC company with 80 missed calls/month losing $6,000+ in recoverable revenue.

Pricing Justification

A receptionist costs $3,000/month, works 40hrs/week, takes breaks, cannot handle two calls at once, does not work nights/weekends. This is under $500/month 24/7. HVAC: 80 missed calls, 5 convert at $1,200 avg = $6,000 recovered. Plumber: 40 missed calls, 5 convert at $300 = $1,500 recovered.

Delivery Process

1. Create client subaccount in GoHighLevel. 2. Go to AI Agents > Voice AI > Create Agent. 3. Set agent name, business name, language, voice (Jessica recommended). 4. Create Knowledge Base using web crawler to scrape client website. 5. Set Agent Goals (collect name, email, contact issue). 6. Link Knowledge Base to agent. 7. Set phone hours under Phone and Availability tab. 8. Enable Advanced Mode > Add Action > Appointment Booking > Select Calendar. 9. Choose time slot count and save. 10. Test in demo environment before going live.

Tools Stack

GoHighLevel ($297-$497/month SaaS mode) - Voice AI agent builder, CRM, automation workflows, calendar booking, SMS follow-up, web crawler for knowledge base training, subaccounts for client management. Jessica voice model recommended.

Client Acquisition

Open Google Maps, find businesses that go to voicemail. Call them, let them hear the AI in action. The missed call log conversation closes most sales.

Outreach Script

You are not selling software, you are selling a missed revenue recovery system. Every dollar they spend on Google, on ads, on referrals is already generating calls that they are not answering. Your system captures that revenue before it walks out the door.

Sales Process

1. Find local business on Google Maps. 2. Call them - if voicemail, they are a prospect. 3. Have the conversation about what they are currently losing. 4. Show the math (missed calls x avg job value = lost revenue). 5. Let them call the AI demo number themselves. 6. Handle objections. 7. Close at $497/month + setup fee.

Objection Handling

Why not hire a receptionist? Costs $3,000/month, works 40hrs, breaks, cannot multitask, no nights/weekends. This is under $500/month 24/7. Does it sound real? Let them call the number themselves - conversation shifts fast.

Contrarian Insight

You do not need to be a marketing expert. You are not promising leads or ad results. You are installing a system like a hot water tank. Most people watching will not take action - less competition for those who do.

Mistake Warning

Most people will not take action. The question is not whether this works, it is whether you will open Google Maps tonight.

Scalability

Test subaccount -> First client via Google Maps outreach -> 10 clients at $497 = $5K MRR -> 20 clients = $9K+ MRR -> GoHighLevel SaaS mode for white-label -> Zero employees, pure systems.

Best Quotes

62% of calls to local businesses go unanswered.
78% of buyers go with the first business that responds to them.
You are not selling software, you are selling a missed revenue recovery system.
He went through his missed call log. 8 out of 12 had already hired someone else that afternoon.

Action Steps

  • Build a demo AI receptionist for a plumber or HVAC company using their website

  • Practice the missed revenue math conversation
  • Let prospects call the demo number themselves

Receptionist: 5 missed calls/week at med spa = $8K/month lost. Charge 20-25%. Speed to lead: 100x conversion in 5 min vs 1 hour. Reactivation: leads already paid for. UGC: replacing $200-$1K creators with $100-$300 AI.

Delivery Process

1. Choose one offer. 2. Identify niche with ROI math. 3. Build with N8N/Make + Retell + Twilio. 4. Receptionist: 24/7 voice, book appointments, FAQs, transfers, spam filter. 5. Reactivation: import CRM, configure outreach. 6. Speed to lead: integrate ads/CRM, trigger 5-min callback. 7. Content: Airtable/Sheets + OpenAI/Claude + scheduling. 8. Hiring: ATS to ClickUp/Notion with screening. 9. UGC: Sora + N8N pipeline. 10. Price per appointment or setup + retainer.

Tools Stack

N8N - automations $5/mo. Retell AI - voice (client pays). Twilio - phone (client pays). OpenAI/Claude - content. Sheets/Airtable - dashboard. Buffer/Hootsuite - scheduling. ClickUp/Notion - tracking. Sora - UGC video. Make.com - alt automation. GHL/HubSpot - CRM. Indeed/LinkedIn - ATS.

Client Acquisition

Cold calling best for receptionist. Approach businesses running ads 6+ months for reactivation. Show 100x conversion study for speed to lead. Build free mockup before pitching.

Outreach Script

References separate cold calling video for receptionist offer. Not provided verbatim here.

Sales Process

1. Identify businesses with pain point. 2. Frame ROI (makes or saves money). 3. Be specific on problem/audience/method. 4. Show mathematical ROI proof. 5. Risk-free performance pricing for reactivation. 6. Close on setup + retainer.

Objection Handling

Performance-based removes risk. Per booked appointment not per close. 5-minute study as proof for speed to lead. Avoid healthcare for content compliance.

Contrarian Insight

Most fail saying 'I do AI automation services' - feature not outcome. Must have clear tangible ROI owners can calculate. Being everything to everyone = nothing to no one. More specific = easier sell + higher price. Per appointment NOT per close.

Mistake Warning

Selling features not outcomes. Not specific enough. Healthcare content (compliance). Performance + setup fee simultaneously as beginner. Slow follow-up.

Scalability

Start with receptionist. Productize content dashboards. Stack offers per client. UGC scales with batch. Hiring creates sticky retainers. Move to monthly retainers.

Best Quotes

It either has to make the business money, or it has to save the business money. That is the filter.
Being everything to everyone means you are being nothing to no one.
One missed call for a roofing company could be a $3,000 job. For a med spa, it can be a $5,000 job.
If you follow up with a lead within 5 minutes, they are 100 times more likely to convert compared to following up an hour later.

Action Steps

  • Week 1: Pick ONE offer (AI receptionist). Self-host N8N. Build demo with Retell + Twilio.
  • Week 2: Calculate ROI for 3 niches (med spas, HVAC, dental). Create one-page pitch.
  • Week 3: Cold call 50 businesses. Track niche response rates.
  • Week 4: Close first client. Document results. Build lead reactivation as upsell.

Full Description

Three-tier AI services model: (1) Education - helping businesses understand what AI is and why they need it, (2) Consulting - identifying where AI can help most in their specific business, (3) Implementation - building and maintaining AI agents like customer support chatbots, WhatsApp lead capture agents, voice agents, and quote generation systems. Built using no-code platforms (Voiceflow, n8n, Relevance AI, Agentiv) so non-coders can deliver. Agents combine 5 components: LLM brain, prompting, memory, external knowledge, and tools/APIs.

Pain Point

Businesses are desperate for AI implementation but have no one to help them. Big consulting firms ignore small businesses. For every AI service provider, there are 1,100+ businesses in the US that need help - a completely untapped market.

Pricing Justification

For every AI service provider there are 1,100 businesses needing help. 50% of employees plan to reorient their business around AI. 66% of employers plan to hire AI-skilled talent. AI-literate employees have 5-10x output.

Delivery Process

1. Identify client needs across education/consulting/implementation. 2. Plan agent using 3 ingredients: Prompting, Knowledge, Tools. 3. Select no-code platform (Voiceflow/Agentiv/n8n/Relevance AI). 4. Build agent: configure LLM, write system prompt, upload knowledge base, connect tools via APIs/schemas. 5. Test and debug using platform transcripts. 6. Deploy to channels: website widget, WhatsApp, Instagram, phone/voice, Telegram, Discord. 7. Monitor and iterate. 8. Maintain and expand.

Tools Stack

Voiceflow: Complex structured agents with visual flow editor. n8n: Workflow automation connecting hundreds of apps. Relevance AI: Custom tool building, creates API endpoints without code. Agentiv (Liams SaaS): Built on OpenAI Assistants API, native WhatsApp/Instagram/Telegram deployment. OpenAI GPT-4/Mini: LLM brains. Airtable: CRM/lead capture. Bland AI: Voice agents. Twilio: Phone provisioning.

Client Acquisition

YouTube content marketing (450K subs), School community (120K members), building in public from day one.

Outreach Script

No cold outreach scripts - acquisition is inbound via YouTube content and community

Sales Process

1. Attract via educational YouTube content. 2. Build trust through transparency. 3. Convert to School community. 4. Upsell to Morningside AI services. 5. Convert to Agentiv SaaS users.

Objection Handling

Shows non-coders can build agents. Reframes AI as opportunity not threat. Naval Ravikant quote: brush up on AI, reapply for the job that rejected you.

Contrarian Insight

You dont need to build the next ChatGPT. The real opportunity is helping existing businesses understand and implement AI. The 3 ingredients framework (Prompting, Knowledge, Tools) is all you need.

Mistake Warning

Thinking you need to be a coder. Not understanding APIs and schemas under the hood even with no-code tools.

Scalability

0 clients: Build 4 agent types from video. 1-5: Offer implementation to small businesses. 5-20: Build repeatable templates. 20-50+: Productize into SaaS (Agentiv 45K users), build community (120K), YouTube flywheel.

Best Quotes

Two years ago, I taught myself how to build AI agents without any prior experience in AI. And since then, Ive started multiple AI businesses that have generated over 5 million in revenue.
For every person or agency offering AI services, there are over 1,100 businesses in the USA alone that need help.
You dont need to build the next ChatGPT. The real opportunity is helping businesses understand and implement AI.
AI literate employees can have 5 to 10x the output of someone without AI literacy.

Action Steps

  • Build the 4 agent types: custom tool (Relevance AI), workflow (n8n), web chat + voice (Voiceflow), WhatsApp (Agentiv)
  • Target small businesses making 500K-10M/year with 3-tier service: education, consulting, implementation
  • Master the 3 ingredients framework and learn API schemas for custom tools
  • Study the School community model - 120K members proves community-led growth works
  • Document your AI learning journey on YouTube

How to Price AI Workflows - Complete Framework		 Consulting Comprehensive pricing guide for AI workflow and automation services. Teaches val Businesses needing AI workflow automation - any business wit Value-based: 10% of annual savings (e.g., $1,200 for $12K annual savings). Starting point for negotiation. $1,500 to $15,000+ per month for ongoing retainers, 3-12 month terms Has tried every pricing model (fixed fee, hou Not detailed in this video - focused on pricing st

Full Description

Comprehensive pricing guide for AI workflow and automation services. Teaches value-based pricing (charge based on business impact, not hours) combined with monthly retainers. Key formula: if workflow saves $12K/year, charge 10% ($1,200) for 10x ROI in first year. Two recommended models: 1) Value-based pricing for initial projects (foot in the door, builds trust), 2) Monthly retainers for ongoing work ($1,500-$15,000/month, 3-12 month terms). Milestone-based retainers position you as consultant vs hourly freelancer. Goal: work toward chief AI officer role within client organizations.

Pain Point

Businesses dont pay for time, they pay for outcomes. Most AI automation providers price on time/effort instead of value delivered. No industry standard pricing exists yet for AI automation services. Businesses need enablement, audits, and education but dont know what AI can do for them.

Pricing Justification

10x ROI rule: client should see 10x return on investment in first year. Walk through math step-by-step to build trust. Example: process costs 1hr/day × $50/hr × 250 days = $12K/year savings. 10% = $1,200 starting price. Plus opportunity cost of freed employee time on higher-value work.

Delivery Process

1. Discovery phase: map entire manual process (frequency, triggers, stakeholders, time per occurrence, hourly value, employees involved). 2. Compare manual vs automated version. 3. Calculate ROI for the automated portion only (dont overpromise). 4. Present value-based price with step-by-step math. 5. Deliver project and build trust. 6. Transition to monthly retainer for ongoing work. 7. Iterate and scale impact over time.

Tools Stack

AI automation/workflow tools (not specified by name), discovery frameworks for mapping manual processes. Emphasizes the consulting methodology over specific tools.

Client Acquisition

Not detailed in this video - focused on pricing strategy

Sales Process

1. Discovery: map full manual process with metrics. 2. Calculate ROI of automation. 3. Present price with transparent math (be ready to explain how you got the number). 4. Close on value-based project. 5. Deliver and build trust. 6. Transition to monthly retainer.

Objection Handling

When client asks how did you get that number - walk through math step-by-step. This builds instant trust. Anchor price on real metrics so it feels like an investment not an expense. Also: ROI compounds over time (month 1: save $1K, month 2: $1.5K, month 3: $2K) because freed time enables higher-value work.

Contrarian Insight

There is currently NO industry standard for pricing AI automation services. Nobody has agreed on the right way to price workflows. This is both a challenge and an opportunity. Also: youd much rather work with one $15K/month client than five $3K/month clients even though total revenue is same - less chaos, deeper relationship, better results, more referrals. Hours-based pricing makes you look like a freelancer; milestone-based positions you as consultant.

Mistake Warning

Pricing based on time/effort instead of outcomes. Also: over-promising results - if you only automate half the process, factor in that half not the full process into your ROI calculation. And: trying to maximize value extraction from each individual project inside a retainer instead of stacking wins and building trust for higher retainers over time.

Scalability

Value-based projects → monthly retainers ($1.5K-$15K/month) → performance bonuses tied to key metrics → chief AI officer positioning within client organizations. Higher retainers over time as impact scales. One deep client relationship beats five shallow ones.

Best Quotes

Businesses dont pay for your time, they pay for outcomes.
There is no industry standard way to price AI automation services yet. Nobody has agreed on the right way.
You should be able to show them exactly how you got to that number. Assume after you tell them the price theyre going to say can you tell me exactly how you got there.
Youd much rather work with one $15,000 per month client than five $3,000 per month clients. Less chaos, less stress, and you get to build a real relationship.

Action Steps

  • Use value-based pricing: charge 10% of first-year savings as starting price point
  • During discovery, map the full manual process with specific metrics (frequency, time, hourly cost, employee count)
  • Walk clients through ROI math step-by-step to build trust and justify pricing
  • Start with value-based projects then transition to $1.5K-$15K/month retainers as trust builds
  • Position as AI consultant/partner not freelancer - use milestone-based deliverables not hourly billing

Monthly maintenance, recurring retainer with builds, or fractional COO subscription (no hour tracking). $72K/month from AI automation agency. $100K+ YouTube tutorials, communities (1,400+ members), d

Full Description

Comprehensive ranking of every AI service rated S-F. S-Tier: Personalized Email Follow-Up, Client Onboarding, Sales Pipeline Follow-Up. A-Tier: Proposal Automation. B-Tier: Reporting/Analytics. C-Tier: Chatbot Lead Capture, Appointment Agents. Key: procedural/linear automations touching sales outperform conversational AI agents.

Pain Point

Slow lead response (396% CVR drop without 60-sec response), poor follow-up, inconsistent onboarding causing churn, manual proposal creation (hours vs minutes).

Pricing Justification

Email Follow-Up: 396% CVR increase from 60-sec response. Pipeline: double revenue improving CVR 15% to 30%. Onboarding: retention compounds revenue. Proposal: hours to minutes while prospect in buying mood.

Delivery Process

1. Identify service tier (S/A/B only). 2. Build on n8n. 3. Integrate client CRM. 4. Connect tools (email, SMS, calendar, doc gen). 5. Configure AI personalization. 6. Test with real data. 7. 1-2 week revision. 8. Transition to subscription. 9. Upsell spider-web systems.

Tools Stack

n8n: Primary automation platform. CRM (HubSpot/Salesforce): Pipeline. PandaDoc/Google Slides: Proposal doc gen. LLM (GPT-4/Claude): AI personalization. Looker Studio/Plecto: Dashboards. SMS/Email: Follow-ups. Apify: $1.20/1K leads. AnyMailFinder: Email discovery. Apollo: Contacts. Instantly/SmartLead: Cold email.

Client Acquisition

YouTube tutorials, communities (1,400+ members), dog-fooding (proposal generator sells proposal generators).

Outreach Script

For SaaS: Hi noticed you were hiring for [role]. I do [thing] using systems. Delivered [result]. Guarantee [X] in 60 days or no pay. Worth a chat? Send 1-3K/week personalized.

Sales Process

1. Use own systems as proof. 2. Build with 1-2 week free revision. 3. Present 3 options: maintenance, $225/hour, or retainer. 4. Use each system for spider-web upsells.

Objection Handling

Dog-fooding: I use proposal generator to sell proposal generators. Revision period reduces risk. Discount for subscription vs hourly.

Contrarian Insight

CONVERSATIONAL AI AGENTS OVERRATED. Chatbots/appointment setters = C-tier despite hype. Convert 15% vs humans 20% - 5% gap on $1K product = $50K loss vs $5K savings. Real money in PROCEDURAL/LINEAR AUTOMATIONS: proposals, email follow-ups, CRM pipeline, onboarding. Boring but profitable.

Mistake Warning

Selling chatbots as primary service. Sound sexy, questionable ROI - worse than humans at critical touchpoint. Sell linear workflow automations instead. Not dog-fooding is a red flag.

Scalability

0-5: S-tier systems as one-time setups. 5-20: Monthly fractional COO (3-15K). Stack spider-web. 20-50+: Template everything, customize per client.

Best Quotes

Respond within 60 seconds, increase conversion by 396%.
Build one system, get five spider web systems to build on top.
I use the proposal generator to sell the proposal generator.
5% conversion gap is more revenue value than the savings from not hiring people.

Action Steps

  • Build S-tier Personalized Email Follow-Up first - 60-second AI-personalized response
  • Build Proposal Automation second - dog-food it to sell itself
  • Avoid chatbots/appointment agents as primary (C-tier)
  • Price: setup + 1-2 week revision, then 3 options: maintenance, $225/hr, or COO subscription
  • Use each system as wedge for spider-web of connected systems

Full Description

Connor Cahill shows his complete AI agency system generating $36K+/month in recurring subscription revenue. Three acquisition methods: Facebook groups, AI content, paid ads ($30/day). All funnel through an AI receptionist demo that sells prospects on the call, then books them. Average $750/month subscription. Detailed math: 10 booked calls/day, 80% show rate, 30% close = 48 new clients/month = $36K MRR. Includes VA delegation at $400/month.

Pain Point

Local businesses need AI but don't know how to implement it. Missing calls, can't follow up, no content presence, no automated marketing.

Pricing Justification

If making $1-3K/day in subscription revenue, $30/day ad spend is trivial. AI demo sells itself on the call. Zero risk for prospect to try.

Delivery Process

1. Post in 3-6 Facebook groups daily 2. Create 3-6 pieces of AI content daily 3. Optionally run $30/day paid ads 4. All channels lead to AI receptionist demo 5. AI demo sells and books appointment 6. Sales call closes at $1,000/month 7. Fulfill with AI tools (receptionist + content + marketing) 8. VA handles posting and fulfillment ($400/month)

Tools Stack

AI receptionist/voice agent, GoHighLevel (CRM, funnels, booking), VSSL (video sales letter of AI selling AI), Facebook groups, paid ads, power dialer for cold calling, referral program system

Client Acquisition

Three high-leverage methods: 1) Facebook groups (post with AI demo number) 2) AI content (3-6 pieces/day) 3) Paid ads ($30/day). Plus cold calling and referral program. One Facebook group post got 70 callers -> 20 booked calls -> 8-9 clients -> $9,500 MRR.

Outreach Script

Facebook group approach: post in 'Business Owners of [City]' groups with AI receptionist phone number. Leads call AI, AI sells them, AI books appointment. One post -> 70 calls -> 20 booked -> 8-9 sales.

Sales Process

1. Prospect calls AI demo from FB group/content/ads 2. AI qualifies and sells 3. AI books appointment or prospect books via landing page 4. Sales call (you or commission rep) 5. Close on $750-$1,000/month subscription 6. Onboard with AI tools

Objection Handling

AI demo handles objections on the call itself. Sales script: AI tells prospect 'The same way I'm trying to sell you is the same way I'm going to be selling for you. Do you not want me to be good at sales?'

Contrarian Insight

Have the AI sell the AI service. The demo IS the pitch. One Facebook group post generated $9,500 in MRR. $30/day ads when making $1-3K/day is obvious math. VA at $400/month handles both acquisition (posting) and fulfillment. Commission-based sales rep gets 50% of first month only - you keep the recurring. With 10% churn, math still reaches $168K MRR in 6 months.

Mistake Warning

Having all three pillars is non-negotiable - missing even one and the model fails. Part 1 + Part 2 but no Part 3 = clients cancel after 30 days. Part 2 + Part 3 but no Part 1 = no clients to retain. Part 1 + Part 3 but no Part 2 = nobody shows up or buys.

Scalability

Post in FB groups -> AI demo sells -> Close on calls -> Hire VA ($400/mo) -> Hire commission sales rep -> Add paid ads ($30/day) -> Remove yourself -> $168K MRR in 6 months

Best Quotes

70 people called the AI receptionist from one Facebook group. I got about 20 booked calls. I got 8 or 9 people to buy. It was like $9,500 a month in subscription revenue from just one Facebook group
The AI is like 'the same way I'm trying to sell you is the same way I'm going to be selling for you. Do you not want me to be good at sales?'
If you have part one and part two but no part three, you'll get clients and they'll cancel after 30 days
$30 to make $2,000 a day. Yeah, obviously that's worth it

Action Steps

  • Find 3 'Business Owners of [City]' Facebook groups in your area
  • Build an AI receptionist demo that can sell your service on the call
  • Create a landing page with VSSL and booking calendar
  • Post in one Facebook group with your AI demo number today
  • Calculate your target: how many booked calls/day to reach $10K MRR?

A-Z AI Agency Build		 Consulting Cameron England pitches his License and Scale program - a full-stack AI agency t Aspiring and existing agency owners. SEO, reputation managem License and Scale program pricing not stated publicly Agency clients: aims for $750+/month average subscription $250K/month agency revenue. Six figures/month YouTube content, Instagram polls, direct pre-selli

Full Description

Cameron England pitches his License and Scale program - a full-stack AI agency training covering self-mastery, offer creation, lead gen, sales, fulfillment, operations, and exit. Guarantees $30K in new MRR or you don't pay. Includes AI tool directory, offer creation agents, ad templates, cold outbound infrastructure, and one-on-one account management. Agency doing $250K/month, still operating.

Pain Point

Stuck in analysis paralysis. Growing but need to delegate. Churning clients. Can't remove self from day-to-day. Pre-ChatGPT agency model is dying. Need systems for fulfillment.

Pricing Justification

Speed: buy speed from someone who's done it. Analogy: would you operate on your own torn ligament? Same logic for building agency with expert guidance.

Delivery Process

1. Self mastery (mindset, daily CEO workflow, weekly sprint) 2. Offer creation (AI-powered offer builder trained on thousands of proven offers) 3. Lead gen (ads, cold outbound, organic content) 4. Sales (closing framework) 5. Fulfillment (AI-leveraged delivery) 6. Scale and remove yourself 7. Exit or cash flow at 50%+ margins

Tools Stack

AI tool directory (offer creation agent, ad templates), paid ads infrastructure, cold outbound systems, GoHighLevel CRM, organic content tools, AI fulfillment automation

Client Acquisition

YouTube content, Instagram polls, direct pre-selling to existing contacts, program referrals

Outreach Script

Pre-sell DM: 'If I built a program covering everything - acquisition, retention, fulfillment - guaranteed your results and worked alongside you to execute with AI helping the process, how much would you pay for that?'

Sales Process

1. Content creates awareness 2. Free value builds trust 3. Direct pitch via YouTube/Instagram 4. Application process 5. Sales call 6. Close with $30K MRR guarantee 7. Onboard with account manager

Objection Handling

Pre-ChatGPT model dying: 'If it was cash flowing and they were removed from it, why would they get rid of it? That's why I still have mine.' Expensive: 'The best investment is a second set of eyes from someone who's done it.' No time: structured so you can implement systematically with account manager support.

Contrarian Insight

Everyone selling courses shut down their agency because they couldn't actually scale it. The pre-ChatGPT agency model is dying. If you're operating under 50% margins, you're building wrong. Self-mastery must come before tactics. Don't buy from people not actively doing what they teach. $30K MRR guarantee because no one who did the work has failed.

Mistake Warning

Learning from people who no longer operate agencies. Skipping self-mastery and going straight to tactics. Operating under 50% margins. Not having all three pillars (lead gen, sales, fulfillment). Expecting overnight results from a program.

Scalability

Self-mastery -> Offer creation -> Lead gen -> Sales -> Fulfillment -> Delegation -> 50%+ margins -> Decentralization -> Exit or cash flow

Best Quotes

I would almost feel bad if I didn't try and sell you this
We have not had a single person that did the work that did not get results
Would you pull out a scalpel and start operating on your own knee?
The pre-ChatGPT agency model is quite simply dying

Action Steps

  • Audit your agency margins - are they above 50%?
  • Identify which pillar is weakest: lead gen, sales, or fulfillment
  • Build a weekly sprint system for CEO-level planning
  • Create an AI-powered offer using ChatGPT + $100M Offers framework
  • Map out your decentralization plan: what needs to happen for the business to run without you
Alex Leischow
AI Voice Cold Caller		 Outbound Alex Leischow builds a fully automated AI outbound voice cold caller using Vapi Local small businesses without websites (scraped from Google Website sale: $1,500-$2,000 per site Not specified - one-time website sales model Not specified for personal income. Model: if Fully automated AI cold calling from scraped Googl

Full Description

Alex Leischow builds a fully automated AI outbound voice cold caller using Vapi + make.com. The agent calls businesses scraped from Google Maps that don't have websites, pitches a pre-built demo website, and collects name/email. Make.com automation triggers calls from a Google Sheet of leads and retrieves call outcomes automatically. Includes prompt engineering, knowledge base setup, and call outcome tracking.

Pain Point

Small businesses don't have websites and are invisible online. Missing digital presence = missing customers. Don't know what their business could look like online.

Pricing Justification

Free demo - zero risk for prospect. Website is already built before the call. They just need to say yes and send email to receive it.

Delivery Process

1. Scrape Google Maps for businesses without websites (~50 cents/50 leads) 2. Build AI voice agent in Vapi with custom prompt 3. Upload knowledge base from your website 4. Build make.com automation to trigger calls from Google Sheet 5. Build second automation to retrieve call outcomes 6. AI calls leads, pitches pre-built website, collects name/email 7. Send demo link to interested leads 8. Close on website purchase

Tools Stack

Vapi (AI voice agent platform), make.com (automation), Google Sheets (lead list + CRM), ChatGPT (prompt writing + knowledge base generation), OpenAI model (Vapi backend), Deepgram (transcription), Google Maps scraper

Client Acquisition

Fully automated AI cold calling from scraped Google Maps data. Zero manual outreach needed.

Outreach Script

AI voice script: 'Hey there. How's your day going? [pause for answer] My name's Alex. I work with a local company called Memberify. We build websites for small businesses. I noticed your business doesn't have a website, so I went ahead and built one for you. No charge or anything. Just wanted to show you what your business could look like online. It's already done. Do you mind if I email you the link real quick so you can take a look?'

Sales Process

1. AI calls from Google Sheet automatically 2. Friendly opener (How's your day?) 3. Pitch: pre-built website already done for them 4. Handle objections conversationally 5. Collect name and email 6. Send demo link 7. Follow up for purchase decision

Objection Handling

Is it free? 'Yep. The preview is totally free. If you like it and want to use it, we can talk about that later.' Hesitant: 'A lot of small businesses in the area don't have a website. We figured it'd be more helpful to show you a finished preview instead of cold pitching.' Not interested: move on to next lead automatically.

Contrarian Insight

Don't start the AI call with a pitch - say 'how's your day going' and wait for response. Leave the 'first message' field empty in Vapi so the bot doesn't speak until the human says hello. Enable end-call function or the bot gets stuck in an infinite goodbye loop. Let ChatGPT write your Vapi prompt (meta: AI writing prompt for AI). Use Perplexity-style knowledge base from your website instead of manual documentation.

Mistake Warning

Having a first message that bombards the lead immediately. Not enabling end-call function (infinite goodbye loop). Making AI responses too long and formal. Not testing the agent yourself before deploying. Forgetting to set up the make.com outcome retrieval automation.

Scalability

Scrape 50 leads -> Build Vapi agent -> Automate calling via make.com -> Sell websites at $1,500-$2,000 -> Scale to hundreds of calls/day -> Add more services beyond websites

Best Quotes

I noticed your business doesn't have a website so I went ahead and built one for you, no charge or anything
If you leave the first message empty, the assistant won't say anything until the lead says hello, which is much more natural
If we didn't have end call on, at the end of the call the bot would get stuck in this loop saying have a great day over and over
We're going to let AI write the prompt for our AI agent. That's fun

Action Steps

  • Sign up for Vapi and create your first voice agent
  • Scrape 50 local businesses without websites from Google Maps
  • Build make.com automation connecting Google Sheet to Vapi for auto-calling
  • Test the agent by calling yourself first
  • Build second make.com automation to retrieve and log call outcomes

Top 5 AI Services Local Businesses Will Buy in 202		 Voice Agent Lee Blue presents a complete system for scaling an AI receptionist agency to 100 ANY local business with a phone. Pizza shops, plumbers, all No explicit setup fee. Focus is on MRR. 1000-2000/month per client. Average 1000/month for math. Scaled to over 100K/month. One Facebook post: THREE channels: 1. Facebook Groups (10/day, free).

Full Description

Lee Blue presents a complete system for scaling an AI receptionist agency to 100K/month. Core offer: white-labeled AI voice receptionist answering calls 24/7, booking appointments, handling inquiries. Three phases: FUEL (Facebook groups + AI avatar content), AI AGENT DEMO (prospects call AI directly and it sells them on booking), CLOSE (sales calls at 1K-2K/month). The AI acts as both product AND sales tool. One Facebook post: 80+ calls, 17 bookings, 9 showed, 6 closed for approx 9500 MRR.

Pain Point

Missing calls after 5pm when competitors closed. Getting put on hold. Not available 24/7. Missing 100% of after-hours demand.

Pricing Justification

Human receptionist 60K/year. AI 12K-24K/year. Being ONLY business open after 5pm captures all after-hours demand. Multiple simultaneous calls. No sick days.

Delivery Process

1. Choose white-label AI platform (GHL, Regal, Acro Neo, Agencies AI, Colon.io). 2. Set up AI with sales-focused prompt. 3. Create AI avatar with HeyGen. 4. Post in 10 Facebook groups/day. 5. Prospects call AI number. 6. AI demos itself while selling. 7. AI sends text with booking link. 8. You/closer take sales call. 9. Close at 1K-2K/month. 10. VA handles fulfillment (1 hour per business). 11. Hire closer at 10% recurring. 12. Hire fuel VA 400/month. 13. Hire fulfillment VA 400/month.

Tools Stack

GoHighLevel - white-label AI caller, 99/month (preferred for margins). HeyGen - AI avatar content. ChatGPT - script generation. Facebook Groups - free lead gen. White-label alternatives: Regal, Acro Neo, Agencies AI, Colon.io. OnlineJobs.ph - VAs at 3-4/hour.

Client Acquisition

THREE channels: 1. Facebook Groups (10/day, free). 2. AI Avatar Content (10 pieces/day via HeyGen). 3. Paid Ads (advanced only). AI receptionist IS the demo - prospects call and experience it.

Outreach Script

FACEBOOK POST: Hey business owners, do you want to be the only business in your area who can take calls after 5pm so when all competition is closed you get 100% of market demand? I have an AI receptionist - 24/7, never misses, sounds human, books to calendar. If you do not believe me, call here [number] and throw it a curveball. AI AVATAR: I want to be your AI receptionist. I take multiple calls at once, never miss, you are the only business open 24/7. After 5pm when competition closes you are the only one. Click below and talk to me.

Sales Process

1. Prospect sees post/content. 2. Calls AI (curiosity + FOMO). 3. AI demos in real-time. 4. AI sells them on why they need it. 5. AI texts booking link. 6. They book call. 7. 30-60 min sales call. 8. Close at 1K-2K/month. 9. Fulfillment VA implements (1 hour).

Objection Handling

If you do not believe me call and throw a curveball - overcome skepticism via experience. AI being impressive IS the objection handler. FOMO: only business open after 5pm.

Contrarian Insight

The AI is not just the product - it is the SALES REP. Prompted to sell during demo. Product demos and sells itself simultaneously. Do not niche down at start - let market tell you. AI prompt quality directly impacts revenue: good prompt = 17/80 book, bad = maybe 10. Future: receptionist saturates, pivot to AI consulting at 10K+.

Mistake Warning

Not making AI prompt good enough at selling. The prompt is the most critical asset. Not posting in enough groups (need 10/day volume). Staying too long on receptionist when market saturates - evolve to consulting.

Scalability

Phase 1: Solo everything. Phase 2: Hire fuel VA + fulfillment VA (400 each). Phase 3: Hire closer (10% recurring). Phase 4: Only do relationships + calls. Phase 5: Stack more AI tools. Future: AI consulting at 10K+ per engagement.

Best Quotes

I posted into one Facebook group. 80 plus people called the AI and it booked 17 onto my calendar. Nine showed up. I closed six.
For very minimal work I was generating 10K per month in revenue which is insane.
This AI caller I prompted and built to be a sales rep for my business.
If you had a really bad agent you might only get 10 people to book - that is 5K in lost potential revenue.

Action Steps

  • Day 1: Set up GHL (99/month). Build AI receptionist with sales prompt. Create HeyGen avatar. Test by calling yourself.
  • Days 2-3: Join 30+ Facebook groups for business owners. Post script with phone number in 10 groups/day.
  • Week 1: Create 10 AI avatar content pieces/day. Post with bio link. Track calls, bookings, shows.
  • Week 2-3: Take all sales calls (30-60 min). Close at 1K-2K/month. After 10 clients identify best niche.
  • Month 2: Hire fuel VA + fulfillment VA (400/month each from OnlineJobs.ph). Hire closer at 10% recurring.

Full Description

A multi-service AI consulting practice offering five distinct services: (1) AI Voice Agents for inbound/outbound call handling, (2) Lead Magnet + Nurture Systems with SMS/email sequences, (3) Social Media Content Automation with AI-generated posts, (4) Customer Referral and Review Systems for exponential growth, and (5) Database Reactivation campaigns that mine existing customer lists for untapped revenue. Each service solves a specific business problem with clear ROI math.

Pain Point

Home services: losing $40K/year from unanswered phones. Real estate: 2-3% lead conversion vs 8-10% for top performers. Lawyers: losing $400K/year from slow lead response. Creators: cannot scale without hiring. All: dormant databases with untapped dollars.

Pricing Justification

Voice agent generated $118K additional revenue for one client. Saved $1,600/month vs call center. Database reactivation: HVAC with 5,000 leads, 5% convert at $3K = $750K revenue from unused database. Real estate: one extra deal = $24K.

Delivery Process

1. Identify business pain point. 2. Build the AI system. 3. Train AI on client business. 4. Connect to existing tools. 5. Test and refine. 6. Launch and monitor. 7. Optimize. 8. Upsell additional services.

Tools Stack

n8n, Make.com, Late/Later (scheduling), Nano Banana Pro (AI visuals), AI voice platforms, SMS/email platforms, CRM integration, Instagram/Facebook Graph API

Client Acquisition

Free School community with 4-week challenge. Pain-point positioning. Referrals from real estate offices. Revenue share with content creators.

Outreach Script

Do not lead with I build AI automation. Lead with I help personal injury lawyers respond faster to leads so they do not lose $400,000 every year to their competition.

Sales Process

1. Identify industry and pain point. 2. Lead with dollar impact. 3. Explain simple fix. 4. Show ROI math. 5. Offer pricing model. 6. Start with one service as foot-in-the-door. 7. Upsell additional services.

Objection Handling

Frame against cost of NOT doing it. Revenue share option removes all risk.

Contrarian Insight

Database reactivation closes highest ticket deals but most builders overlook it. Revenue share with content creators is a gold mine most miss - leverage someone else s audience instead of finding clients from scratch. The hard part is not technology, it is understanding business problems.

Mistake Warning

Pricing based on time to build instead of value created. Leading with technology instead of business problem.

Scalability

Start with one service -> Land first client -> Upsell additional services -> Add revenue share deals with creators -> Stack 4+ industries -> Revenue share creates passive income layer.

Best Quotes

I built an outbound AI voice agent that generated an additional $118,000.
Every time he uses the system with one of his clients, I get 20%. He does 40 packages per month, I make $4,000.
Database reactivation consistently closes at the highest ticket rate.
Do not lead with I build AI automation. Lead with I help personal injury lawyers respond faster.

Action Steps

5 AI Services To Sell For 5000 in 2026		 Automation Charlie Barber outlines 5 proven AI services: (1) AI Lead Reactivation and Outre Service 1: Med spas, coaches, info products. Service 2: Real A few thousand dollars per service. Low barrier to entry for reactivation. Content strategist replacement: 2K/month. Retention: ongoing. Sales analysis: weekly reports. 5000 new Instagram followers/month. Pays 2K/m Cold email campaigns. School.com outreach with Loo

Full Description

Charlie Barber outlines 5 proven AI services: (1) AI Lead Reactivation and Outreach - automated DM/email to old leads using MessengerFlow, AutoLeads, Instantly.ai; (2) AI Content Operator - avatar content with HeyGen + Descript + ManyChat + trial reels for 5000 new followers/month; (3) RevOps - connecting marketing/sales/fulfillment into one AI pipeline, diagnosing 3 leak points (lead-to-booking, call-to-close, close-to-onboarding); (4) SaaS Retention and Churn Reduction - automated follow-up messaging to increase LTV; (5) AI Sales and Conversion Agent - AI reviews sales calls/DMs/emails to identify objections and patterns, improving close rates 10%+.

Pain Point

Missing 30K-100K/year from unfollowed leads. Content inconsistency. Revenue leaking between stages. Customer churn. 10% close rate improvement at 10K/deal = 100K extra.

Pricing Justification

Reactivation: 30-100K unused in old leads. Content: replaces 2K/month human. RevOps: fewer leaks = more revenue. Retention: increases LTGP. Sales: 10% on 100 deals at 10K = 100K extra.

Delivery Process

Outreach: 1. Set up MessengerFlow/AutoLeads/Instantly. 2. Import old leads from CRM. 3. Create attractive offer. 4. Launch automated outreach. 5. AI responds via GHL. 6. Book appointments. Content: 1. LA10 for research. 2. Script with AI. 3. Clone owner with HeyGen. 4. Edit with Descript. 5. Test 5 hooks on trial reels. 6. Post winner to main. 7. ManyChat comment automation. 8. Notion pipeline. RevOps: 1. Diagnostic call. 2. ID worst leak. 3. Build automation. Sales: 1. Connect Fireflies. 2. N8N + LLM analysis. 3. Summarize calls. 4. Weekly reports + Slack recaps.

Tools Stack

MessengerFlow - Facebook DMs. AutoLeads.app - Instagram outreach. Instantly.ai - cold email. LA10 - content research. HeyGen - avatar cloning. Descript - AI video editing. ManyChat - comment automation. GoHighLevel - CRM/AI responses. Notion - pipeline. N8N - automation backbone. Fireflies - call recording. Slack - recaps. Claude/GPT - analysis. School.com - prospecting.

Client Acquisition

Cold email campaigns. School.com outreach with Loom VSSL (few minutes). Funnel: outreach > Loom > booked call > close.

Outreach Script

Framework: reach out on School.com, send short Loom VSSL focused on end results not mechanisms. Always sell the destination not the journey.

Sales Process

1. Outreach on School.com or cold email. 2. Short Loom VSSL on end results. 3. Funnel to booked call. 4. Act as doctor - diagnostic questions. 5. ID specific problem. 6. Mold offer to their problems. 7. Present ROI-focused solution. 8. Close.

Objection Handling

Act as doctor - morally wrong to prescribe without diagnosing. Ask questions first. Lead with value. Sell destination not journey. Show personal proof (I pay 2K/month for this myself).

Contrarian Insight

RevOps is SaaS term moving downstream - get on it early. Do not need Meta ads (high learning curve) - outreach is lower barrier. AI replaces 2K/month content strategists. Trial reels strategy: test 5 hooks on trial reels (new audience), post winner to main profile. You must look the part - optimize outreach profile for target niche.

Mistake Warning

Not knowing niche deeply enough. Not looking the part on profiles. Selling mechanisms instead of outcomes. Trying everything instead of diagnosing ONE leak. Not testing hooks before posting.

Scalability

Start reactivation (lowest barrier). Build to RevOps. Add content operator. Layer sales analysis for high-ticket. Each service compounds.

Best Quotes

Most businesses are missing out on 30 to 100K per year just because they are not following up with past customers.
Always sell the destination, not the journey.
Be just like a doctor. Get on a sales call. Ask questions. Mold yourself to their problems. Lead with value. That is how you build a real business.
A 10% improvement in close rate on 100 deals per year at 10K each can mean 100K in extra revenue.

Action Steps

  • Week 1: Choose reactivation or RevOps. Set up MessengerFlow + AutoLeads + Instantly. Create optimized outreach profile.
  • Week 2: Cold email 100 businesses. Send Loom VSSL under 3 minutes focused on results. Track responses.
  • Week 3: Diagnostic calls. ID leak points. Build first automation with N8N/GHL. Document results.
  • Week 4: Add content operator. Set up HeyGen + Descript + ManyChat. Test trial reels for one client.
  • Week 5: Layer sales analysis for high-ticket clients. Connect Fireflies + N8N + LLM for automated call analysis.

AATES / Bill (VP Strategic Partnerships)
AI layoff headlines are lies - companies lay off to appease Wall Street or ship jobs overseas. AI is coming for tasks, not entire jobs.
Cook AI / Serge
Even with the best AI operating system, youll fail without knowing the right market. Execution speed without market truth = death sooner.
Spencer (web design agency)
Build the website BEFORE the cold call - dont pitch a service, show a finished product. The lead magnet IS the deliverable.
Tech With Tim
Claude Code is not the best by a mile like YouTubers claim. OpenClaw on VPS is more security risk than productivity tool if set up wrong.
unknown (email marketing reviewer)
AI email tools produce generic content lacking brand voice; still need human review. Advanced AI features come at premium prices.
unknown (small business AI advisor)
Chatbots have a bad rap but with right data they mean the difference between a sale and a lost prospect. Only 2-3% of visitors convert without AI behavior analysis.
Declan (GHL/AI agency)
Speed to value beats everything. Unlike websites/ads/SMMA that take weeks, AI receptionist shows value within hours. Sticky = painful to remove = guaranteed retention.
unknown (micro-SaaS educator)
Build review-exchange clubs where users buy each others products and leave reviews - bootstraps social proof. Run the AI agent yourself to publish 400-600 ebooks/month on Gumroad.

Gym Members Now
Dont solve one problem - sell complete system. One service = low price. Full system = 5-10x more. Roll up agencies into portfolio to sell for 5-10x more than solo exit.
Adam (Six Flow / VoiceAI Business Academy)
Dont pitch service on cold calls - offer free lead magnet. Using lead magnets gives internal confidence (giving not taking), reduces call reluctance, improves tonality, closes more.
Liam Ottley (ft. Nate Herk)
APIs are THE keystone skill - not AI itself. Biggest hurdle is headers/authentication. Use Postman workshops first. Cant teach obsession - thats the secret sauce.
Christian (Bond founder)
5% success rate on products (Peter Levels). Buy boring Boomer businesses with seller financing (no cash upfront), inject AI to cut labor. Boring acquisition beats building from scratch.
unknown (BuildMyAgent tutorial)
Lead magnet IS the agents output. Instead of static PDF, AI creates truly personalized deliverable per lead - higher perceived value while fully automated.
White Label Suite / Walt
Dont sell GoHighLevel as a CRM. Sell a complete end-to-end lead generation service with AI voice, outreach, and nurturing packaged at $4K/mo.
unknown (agency SaaS educator)
Stop looking like just another agency - start looking like a tech company with infrastructure. Infrastructure = retention = MRR. Dont stack 5 tools. Pick ONE, create ONE offer, sell ONE transformation.
James Oaks (via Jasper GHL community)
Forget closing sales - learn to OPEN them. Quality over quantity: 300 calls with 8% close rate beats thousands of spray-and-pray calls. Meet prospects in person - invite them to lunch, your home office. No free trials ever.
Shiny AI (agency)
Dont run one campaign directly to leads. Use two campaigns: first farms clicks (80% budget) to build familiarity, second retargets for actual meetings (20%). After seeing you repeatedly across platforms, you seem like a huge established company.
unknown (e-commerce reviewer)
E-commerce needs a platform specifically built for online stores, not generic email tools. Product pickers and coupons auto-pulled from your cart is the differentiator.
unknown (AI agency niche ranking)
The niches everyone recommends on YouTube (e-commerce, drop shipping, restaurants) are the ones you should AVOID. Use 5-criteria framework: LTV>$3K, obvious pain, decision maker access, 30-day visible ROI, no compliance.
unknown (AI receptionist seller)
Use the AI receptionist as its own sales tool - let prospects call it and experience the demo. The AI literally sells them on why they need AI. One Facebook group post generated 77 calls, 35 booked calls, and 15 closes.
unknown (AI OFM agency)
Worst AI models can hit 1K faster than perfect ones because people spend 3 months perfecting models while putting zero time into marketing. Dont sign up as a company before making a penny. Outsource low-ROI tasks immediately.
